myth.un: If something nasty happens online, the kindest thing is to delete it all so we can forget it.
myth.re: Deleting wipes the proof needed to act; calmly keep screenshots and chats as evidence, then report it.
myth.why: Without evidence, the people who can stop the abuser have little to work with.

scenarios.relearn: Don't delete in a panic; calmly keep evidence (screenshots, chats) and report online abuse to cybercrime 1930.

scenarios.source: silence can be a danger sign
scenarios.hook: "My child suddenly hides the screen and went secretive, but that's just normal teenage privacy."

myth.un: My child suddenly hides the screen and went secretive, but that's just normal teenage privacy.
myth.re: New fear, hiding the screen or sudden secrecy online can be a sign something is wrong; check in gently and stay the open door.
myth.why: Sudden online secrecy can mean a child is being pressured or threatened.

scenarios.relearn: Sudden online secrecy or screen-hiding deserves a gentle check-in, not a shrug; stay the open, tellable door.

scenarios.hook: "Whatever happens on a screen isn't real, so online stuff can't really hurt my child."

myth.un: Whatever happens on a screen isn't real, so online stuff can't really hurt my child.
myth.re: Online grooming, exploitation and sextortion cause real fear and harm; treat an online threat as seriously as one in person.
myth.why: The fear and coercion a child feels online are entirely real.

scenarios.relearn: Online grooming, exploitation and sextortion are real harm; take an online threat as seriously as one in person.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a grooming red flag online, or an ordinary one?

items.text: An adult online asks your child to keep their chats a secret
A classmate messages about tomorrow's homework
An online 'friend' sends gifts and recharge codes
A cousin shares a funny video in the family group
A new contact tries to move chat to a private, hidden app
A teammate in a game says 'good match, play tomorrow?'

scenarios.relearn: Secrecy, gifts and hidden chats are flags; homework and game chat are ordinary.

scenarios.hook: Your child shows you a scary online message. Sort each reaction: protective, or risky?

items.text: Thank them calmly for showing you
Shout and grab the phone in anger
Save screenshots before anything is deleted
Tell them it's their own fault for chatting
Report it to cybercrime 1930
Make them promise never to mention it again

scenarios.relearn: Stay calm, keep evidence and report; anger, blame and forced silence push a child to hide the next danger.

scenarios.hook: Sort: staying close and tellable, or surveillance-as-control that backfires?

items.text: Asking with interest who they game and chat with
Secretly reading every private message
Agreeing on which apps are okay together
Threatening to track their location all day
'Tell me about anyone online who makes you uneasy'
Punishing them for any new app you didn't approve

scenarios.relearn: Interest, shared rules and an open invite keep a child tellable; spying and punishment make them hide.

scenarios.hook: Sort: safe to share with an online contact your child just met, or keep private?

items.text: Your home address and which school they attend
A favourite cartoon character
Live location and when the house is empty
That they like cricket
Private photos of themselves
Their nickname in a public game

scenarios.relearn: Address, school, live location and private photos stay private with a new online contact; harmless likes are fine.

scenarios.hook: Your child confides about something that went wrong online. Sort: believing, or blaming?

items.text: 'I'm glad you told me, this isn't your fault'
'You should have known better than to reply'
'We'll sort this out together'
'What did you do to make them do that?'
'You're not in trouble for telling me'
'This is why I never trusted you online'

scenarios.relearn: 'It's not your fault, you're not in trouble, we'll sort it together' keeps a child talking; blame shuts them down.

scenarios.hook: Sort each situation: report mainly via cybercrime 1930, or reach for Childline 1098?

items.text: A stranger online is pressuring your child for photos
Your child needs to talk to a child-help counsellor
Someone is threatening to leak your child's images
You want child-protection guidance and support
An account is sextorting your child for money
A frightened child needs a caring helpline to call

scenarios.relearn: Grooming, leaks and sextortion go to cybercrime 1930; child support to Childline 1098.

scenarios.hook: Sort each parent move online: builds safety, or leaves a child exposed?

items.text: Keeping screens in shared family spaces
Letting a young child video-call unknown adults alone
Talking about online tricks before they happen
Assuming a kids' app needs no supervision
Knowing how and where to report
Ignoring who your child meets in games

scenarios.relearn: Shared-space screens, early talk and knowing how to report build safety; unsupervised calls and ignoring contacts expose.

scenarios.hook: Sort each online-safety belief: a true one to keep, or a myth to drop?

items.text: A sextorted child is a victim, never at fault
If they sent a photo, it's their own problem
Keep evidence, then report online abuse
Online harm isn't real because it's just a screen
An online 'friend' earning secrecy is a red flag
Strangers are the only online danger

scenarios.relearn: Victims aren't at fault, keep evidence and report, secrecy is a flag; the rest are myths.

scenarios.hook: Your son Yuvraj, 10, says a new gaming friend wants to chat on a private app and keep it secret.

steps.prompt: He mentions it casually while playing. What do you do?

options.text: Thank him, and calmly talk it through
options.then: Yuvraj pauses the game. 'He's really nice though,' he says.

options.text: Snatch the device away and ban all games as punishment
options.then: He cries, and later plays at a friend's house without telling you.

options.text: Say it's probably just another kid, so it's fine
options.then: He downloads the app that night.

options.text: Tell him to say no, and leave it there
options.then: He agrees, but doesn't understand why it matters.

steps.why: Calm thanks keeps him telling you about contacts like this.

steps.prompt: Yuvraj says the friend gives him free game coins and calls him special. What do you explain?

options.text: Gifts plus secrecy online is a warning sign
options.then: He thinks. 'So a real friend wouldn't need it to be secret?'

options.text: Everyone online is a bad person
options.then: He rolls his eyes and stops listening.

options.text: Free coins are fine. Just never give your address
options.then: He nods, and keeps accepting the coins.

options.text: You should have known better than to trust him
options.then: He goes quiet and looks ashamed.

steps.why: Naming the red flags calmly helps him spot grooming himself.

steps.prompt: The friend keeps messaging, pushing Yuvraj to chat privately. What do you do?

options.text: Save the chats, block, and report to cybercrime 1930
options.then: Yuvraj helps you take screenshots, and the report is logged.

options.text: Reply pretending to be Yuvraj, to try and catch him out
options.then: The friend gets suspicious and deletes his account.

options.text: Block him and delete the chats
options.then: He's gone, and so is the record of what he did.

options.text: Let Yuvraj handle it, since he knows now
options.then: Yuvraj replies 'no', and the friend tries a new approach.

steps.why: Saving evidence and reporting help stop him targeting other children.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, Yuvraj mentions another player asked for his photo. What do you do?

options.text: Thank him, and look at the chat with him calmly
options.then: He shows you the chat. 'I said no, like we talked about.'

options.text: Take his games away, since this keeps happening
options.then: He hands the device over and stops mentioning chats.

options.text: Tell him he should handle these himself by now
options.then: He nods, and deals with the next one alone.

options.text: Say kids ask for photos all the time
options.then: He shrugs and goes back to his game.

steps.why: Each calm response keeps him telling you the next time.

scenarios.debrief: A new contact pushing secret private chat is a grooming flag, so coach your child calmly and report it.
scenarios.relearn: Secret private chat with a new contact is a grooming flag; coach calmly.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Nisha, 16, says someone online is threatening to share a private photo unless she pays.

steps.prompt: She's shaking and can hardly speak. What do you do?

options.text: Say it's not her fault, and you'll face it together
options.then: Nisha breaks down, relieved. 'I thought you'd hate me.'

options.text: Ask how she could ever send a photo like that
options.then: She stops talking and stares at the floor.

options.text: Take her phone away and ground her for the whole month
options.then: She hands it over and goes silent, sure she's the one being punished.

options.text: Promise her you'll make it all go away tonight
options.then: She nods, though you have no idea yet how you'll do that.

steps.why: Sextortion is never the child's fault. She needs to hear that first.

steps.prompt: The person sets a deadline and demands money within the hour. What do you do?

options.text: Don't pay, and stop replying
options.then: The deadline passes. More threats arrive, but you've stopped feeding them.

options.text: Pay quietly to make it disappear
options.then: They take the money and ask for more the next day.

options.text: Try to negotiate a smaller amount
options.then: They agree, then come back with a new demand.

options.text: Threaten them back to scare them off
options.then: They send more threats, faster now.

steps.why: Paying invites more demands. Stopping contact takes away their power.

steps.prompt: The messages keep coming. What do you do with them?

options.text: Save messages and usernames, not the photo
options.then: You save the usernames, messages and payment details, but not the photo.

options.text: Delete them all to protect Nisha
options.then: The threats are gone from her phone, and so is the evidence.

options.text: Forward them to relatives and ask for advice
options.then: The photo's existence becomes family gossip.

options.text: Delete all her accounts so she can start fresh
options.then: She's harder to reach, but there's no record left to report.

steps.why: Evidence is what helps stop the person and protect her.

steps.prompt: Nisha begs you not to involve anyone official. What do you say?

options.text: We'll report to cybercrime 1930. You're the victim
options.then: She cries, but nods when you promise to stay by her side.

options.text: Okay. We'll keep this just between the two of us
options.then: Nisha relaxes, and the person keeps messaging her.

options.text: You should have thought of that before you sent it
options.then: She runs to her room and slams the door.

options.text: Let's wait and see if they give up on their own
options.then: A week later, the person finds her on a new app.

steps.why: Reporting to cybercrime 1930 treats her as a victim and helps stop it.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, Nisha still feels she brought it on herself. What do you tell her?

options.text: The blackmailer did this. You're not to blame
options.then: Nisha nods slowly and says she's glad she told you.

options.text: Let's put it all behind us now and move on
options.then: She nods, and carries the shame quietly.

options.text: Just be much more careful online from now on
options.then: She hears that it was her carelessness.

options.text: Everyone makes mistakes like this at your age
options.then: She shrugs, still believing it was mostly her fault.

steps.why: The fault is always the blackmailer's. She needs to hear it again and again.

scenarios.debrief: With sextortion, reassure your child it's not their fault, keep evidence, never pay, and report to cybercrime 1930.
scenarios.relearn: Sextortion: reassure, keep evidence, never pay, report to cybercrime 1930.

scenarios.hook: You find your son Kiaan, 6, on a video call with an adult 'fan' he met on a kids' app.

steps.prompt: Kiaan is giggling at the screen. What do you do?

options.text: End the call gently and stay calm
options.then: Kiaan looks up. 'He was nice. He liked my dance.'

options.text: Scream at him and smash the tablet
options.then: Kiaan bursts into tears and hides under the bed.

options.text: Let the call finish so he isn't upset
options.then: The man asks Kiaan to call again tomorrow, just the two of them.

options.text: Grab the tablet and scold him
options.then: Kiaan cries and promises never again, but keeps glancing at the tablet.

steps.why: A calm end to the call protects him without frightening him.

steps.prompt: At dinner, Kiaan asks if he can call his new friend again tomorrow. What do you say?

options.text: No. Grown-ups we don't know shouldn't call kids
options.then: He thinks. 'Even nice ones?' 'Even nice ones,' you say.

options.text: Not after the very bad thing you did today
options.then: His lip trembles. 'I'm sorry, Mumma.'

options.text: No, because I said so. That's the end of it
options.then: He sulks and asks again at bedtime.

options.text: Never. He might be a very bad man, beta
options.then: Kiaan's eyes go wide, and he won't sleep alone that night.

steps.why: A simple, calm rule keeps him safe without scaring or blaming him.

steps.prompt: That night, you look at the app and the man's profile. What do you do?

options.text: Save screenshots and report to cybercrime 1930
options.then: The helpline takes the details, and you remove the app together.

options.text: Delete the app and hope that's the end of it
options.then: The app is gone, but the man is still calling other children.

options.text: Ban Kiaan from all screens for good after this
options.then: Kiaan watches cartoons at a neighbour's house instead.

options.text: Message the man yourself and warn him off
options.then: He blocks you and keeps using the app.

steps.why: Reporting protects Kiaan and other children the man may be calling.

scenarios.debrief: Adults can reach children inside kids' apps, so end the contact calmly, talk, and report, without terrifying your child.
scenarios.relearn: Adults can reach kids in 'kids' apps, so end the contact calmly and talk without terrifying your child.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Meher, 14, admits she sent a photo to an online friend, and now she feels sick about it.

steps.prompt: She can't look at you and waits for your reaction. What do you say first?

options.text: How could you trust a stranger online with something like that?
options.then: Meher goes silent and says she has already deleted the chat.

options.text: You're grounded, and the phone stays with me
options.then: She hands it over without a word and shuts her door.

options.text: It's not the end, and it's not your fault. We'll handle it
options.then: Meher's shoulders drop, and she starts crying as she hands you the phone.

options.text: It's okay. Just delete the chat and we'll forget it
options.then: Meher deletes it all with shaking hands, and the account is still out there.

steps.why: Leading with 'not your fault' lifts the shame, so she keeps talking to you.

steps.prompt: Next morning a message arrives from the same person, asking for another photo. What do you do?

options.text: Screenshot the chat and the profile before anything else
options.then: You save the account name, the messages and the times in one folder.

options.text: Reply as Meher and warn them to stop
options.then: The reply is a veiled threat, and now the sender knows an adult is watching.

options.text: Delete the app from her phone right away
options.then: The app is gone, and so is the chat you would need to show anyone.

options.text: Block the account for now and keep a close eye on her phone
options.then: The messages stop for now, and nothing is saved if the sender comes back.

steps.why: Saved proof is what lets a report be acted on.

steps.prompt: Meher asks, very quietly, whether you have to tell anyone. What do you say?

options.text: No one ever needs to know. I promise
options.then: Meher looks relieved, and nothing reaches anyone who could stop the sender.

options.text: Yes. We'll report it to cybercrime 1930, and I'll be with you
options.then: She nods slowly and asks if she can sit next to you during the call.

options.text: Only if he contacts you again after today
options.then: She agrees, and the report now waits on a stranger's next move.

options.text: Let's wait a few days and see whether they give up on their own
options.then: Meher agrees, and the account still holds her photo.

steps.why: Reporting to 1930 brings in people who can act, and she has you beside her.

steps.prompt: A week on, Meher is quieter than usual and skips her friends' group chat. What do you do?

options.text: Bring up the photo again so she learns something from it
options.then: Meher's face closes, and she mutters that she already knows.

options.text: Leave it alone. Talking will only upset her
options.then: The house stays calm, and Meher keeps whatever she's feeling to herself.

options.text: Take her out for ice cream and a film to take her mind off it
options.then: She smiles for an hour, and the heavy feeling is back by bedtime.

options.text: Tell her it wasn't her fault, and that you're still here
options.then: She leans on you for a moment and says she keeps replaying it.

steps.why: Saying 'not your fault' after the crisis helps the shame fade.

scenarios.debrief: When a child regrets what they sent, lead with 'not your fault', keep evidence, get help, not shame.
scenarios.relearn: Meet an online regret with 'not your fault', keep evidence and get help, not shame.

scenarios.hook: Late at night, you see your cousin Sunil messaging your son Kabir, 11, and asking him to keep their chats secret.

steps.prompt: Kabir is asleep and his phone is on the table. What do you do tonight?

options.text: Tell yourself Sunil is family and means nothing by it
options.then: You put the phone down, and the word 'secret' keeps nagging at you.

options.text: Call Sunil right now and shout at him
options.then: Sunil laughs it off, and by morning he has told Kabir to delete the chat.

options.text: Screenshot the chats and plan a calm talk with Kabir tomorrow
options.then: You lie awake for a while, but you have the messages and a plan.

options.text: Wake Kabir up gently right now and ask him what's been going on
options.then: Kabir wakes frightened, thinks he's in trouble, and says it's nothing.

steps.why: Saving what you saw and waiting for a calm moment protects Kabir without scaring him.

steps.prompt: Next morning Kabir is eating breakfast before school. How do you bring it up?

options.text: Say you saw the chats and that he's not in trouble
options.then: Kabir hesitates, then says Sunil uncle sends him game credits.

options.text: Ask him why he's been hiding these chats from you
options.then: Kabir flushes, says he wasn't hiding anything, and leaves early.

options.text: Say nothing, and check his phone every night instead
options.then: Kabir has no idea you've seen anything, and the chats carry on.

options.text: Tell him he's not to talk to Sunil uncle any more
options.then: Kabir looks confused and asks why, and you don't know what to say.

steps.why: Opening with 'you're not in trouble' makes it safe for him to tell you more.

steps.prompt: That weekend you set a family rule about chats with adults. What is the rule?

options.text: Only chat with relatives you know well
options.then: Kabir points out that Sunil uncle is a relative he knows well.

options.text: No phone after eight at night, full stop
options.then: Kabir sulks, and the rule says nothing about secrets.

options.text: No adult should ever ask you to keep secrets from us
options.then: Kabir nods slowly and says Sunil uncle told him the opposite.

options.text: Tell us straight away if anyone is ever rude to you online
options.then: Kabir agrees, though Sunil uncle has only ever been nice to him.

steps.why: A clear 'no adult asks you for secrets' rule removes the tool groomers rely on, even in the family.

steps.prompt: A few days later, Kabir shows you a new message from Sunil, offering game credits if he keeps it secret. What do you do?

options.text: Thank Kabir, save it, and report it to cybercrime 1930 or Childline 1098
options.then: The person on the line takes the details and explains what happens next.

options.text: Tell Sunil firmly that you don't allow private chats with kids
options.then: Sunil's smile tightens. He deletes his side, and no one who can act ever sees it.

options.text: Accuse him of grooming Kabir in front of the whole family
options.then: Relatives go quiet, Sunil acts wounded, and the family takes his side.

options.text: Block Sunil's number, and keep it in the family to avoid a fuss
options.then: The messages stop on Kabir's phone, and Sunil can still reach other children.

steps.why: It's never Kabir's fault. An adult pushing secrets is for 1930 or 1098 to assess, and your saved chats help.

scenarios.debrief: The known-adult risk works online; a relative earning private secrecy is a flag.
scenarios.relearn: The known-adult risk works online, so check in calmly and never dismiss it.

scenarios.source: coach moved chat off the group
scenarios.hook: Your daughter Anaya's tuition teacher has started messaging only her, away from the class group.

steps.prompt: Anaya says he just sends extra notes and compliments. What do you do?

options.text: Ask him to keep messages in the class group, and ask why
options.then: He replies that Anaya is gifted and needs extra attention.

options.text: Feel proud that he's singled her out
options.then: You praise Anaya, and the private chat grows longer each week.

options.text: Pull Anaya out of tuition that same day
options.then: Anaya is upset to lose her classes, and he keeps messaging her anyway.

options.text: Ask Anaya to show you all of his chats every night before bed
options.then: Anaya hands over her phone each night, and the one-to-one chat carries on.

steps.why: Moving contact back into a visible group removes the privacy grooming needs.

steps.prompt: A week later the teacher offers Anaya free classes at his home, just for her. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, since free help is hard to turn down
options.then: Anaya starts going alone on Saturdays, and he asks her not to mention it.

options.text: Accept, but drop her off and pick her up from his home yourself
options.then: You wait outside each time, and the classes behind his door carry on.

options.text: Say no to classes alone, and ask about the group batch
options.then: He says the group batch is full, and doesn't offer anything else.

options.text: Post about him in the parents' WhatsApp group
options.then: Other parents argue in the group, and the teacher hears about it by evening.

steps.why: Special favours that lead to alone time are a flag, however generous they seem.

steps.prompt: That weekend you ask Anaya about her tuition teacher, and she asks why you want to know. What do you say?

options.text: Because I don't trust male teachers at all
options.then: Anaya rolls her eyes, and the real reason never comes across.

options.text: No reason. I'm just curious
options.then: Anaya shrugs and goes back to her phone.

options.text: Adults shouldn't need private chats with kids. Tell me anything
options.then: Anaya thinks, then says he told her not to show you some messages.

options.text: Because I love you, beta, and I worry about you more than you know
options.then: Anaya hugs you, but she still doesn't know what should worry her.

steps.why: Naming the flag in plain words helps her spot it and tell you.

steps.prompt: The next evening, Anaya shows you messages the teacher told her to hide from you. What do you do?

options.text: Say it's not her fault, save the chat, and call cybercrime 1930
options.then: Anaya sits close while you make the call, and her shoulders drop.

options.text: Message the teacher yourself and demand an explanation
options.then: He deletes his side of the chat and says it was all about homework.

options.text: Delete the chats and block him, so she's rid of him for good
options.then: He's blocked, and the proof anyone could act on is gone.

options.text: Ask her why she didn't show you these messages sooner
options.then: Anaya's eyes fill, and she says he told her you'd be angry.

steps.why: Telling her it's not her fault, then saving and reporting, protects her and keeps her telling you.

scenarios.debrief: Private one-to-one contact and special favour are grooming flags; keep adult-child chat visible.
scenarios.relearn: Private one-to-one contact and special favour are grooming flags online.

scenarios.hook: Your son Ishaan, 12, runs to you with his phone. A stranger has just sent him a creepy message.

steps.prompt: He's nervous about how you'll react. What do you do first?

options.text: Thank him for showing you so fast, and stay calm
options.then: Ishaan lets out a breath and turns the screen so you can both read it.

options.text: Look disgusted and take the phone away for a month
options.then: Ishaan's face falls, and he says he should never have shown you.

options.text: Ask why a stranger can even message him
options.then: Ishaan gets defensive and says he didn't do anything.

options.text: Tell him it's nothing and delete it for him
options.then: Ishaan looks unsure, and the message is gone before anyone saved it.

steps.why: Calm thanks shows him that telling you works, so he'll do it again.

steps.prompt: An hour later, a second message arrives from the same account. What do you do?

options.text: Screenshot it all, block the account and report it together
options.then: Ishaan watches you save it and asks what happens to the sender.

options.text: Reply to the account and threaten to go straight to the police
options.then: The account mocks you, then vanishes and takes the chat with it.

options.text: Just block it and move on
options.then: The messages stop, and nothing is saved if the account returns.

options.text: Screenshot it, and leave it at that
options.then: The proof is saved, and the account is free to message other children.

steps.why: Saving, blocking and reporting together keeps him involved and safe.

steps.prompt: At dinner, Ishaan's younger sister asks what happened. What do you say?

options.text: Nothing. It's not for little ears
options.then: His sister pouts, and Ishaan looks as if he's done something shameful.

options.text: Ishaan got into trouble on his phone
options.then: Ishaan glares at you and pushes his food around.

options.text: Someone online sent Ishaan something creepy, so you be careful too
options.then: His sister nods, hearing a warning but not that telling you works.

options.text: Ishaan showed me a stranger's odd message at once. I'm proud of him
options.then: Ishaan grins at his plate, and his sister says she'd tell too.

steps.why: Praising him in front of others teaches both kids that telling you pays off.

scenarios.debrief: Reward fast telling with calm thanks; punishing the messenger teaches a child to hide.
scenarios.relearn: Reward fast telling with calm thanks; punishing the messenger makes them hide.

scenarios.hook: Someone online has been sending your daughter Zoya nasty messages for a week, and she has finally told you.

steps.prompt: The messages are still on her phone. What do you do first?

options.text: Delete everything at once so Zoya never has to see those words again
options.then: Zoya's screen is clear, and so is the proof of what was sent.

options.text: Reply to the account and demand that they stop at once
options.then: The account replies with worse, then deletes its side of the chat.

options.text: Report the account using the app's own button, and wait
options.then: The app sends an automatic reply, and the messages keep coming.

options.text: Screenshot the messages, dates and profile before anything else
options.then: It takes twenty minutes, and every message is now saved in one folder.

steps.why: Proof saved first means a report can actually be acted on.

steps.prompt: Zoya asks if you're going to make this bigger than it is. What do you say?

options.text: This isn't your fault, and reporting it is how it stops
options.then: Zoya bites her lip, then nods and says okay.

options.text: Yes, because you should have told me a week ago
options.then: Zoya's eyes fill, and she says this is exactly why she didn't.

options.text: No. We'll ignore it for now, and it will die down on its own
options.then: Zoya looks relieved, and another message arrives that night.

options.text: Only if it keeps going after the weekend
options.then: Zoya agrees, and the weekend brings three more messages.

steps.why: She needs to hear it's not her fault before she can back the report.

steps.prompt: That evening, after yet another message, you decide to report it. Where do you take it?

options.text: Her school, since the sender might be a classmate
options.then: The school says it can't act on messages from an unknown account.

options.text: The family WhatsApp group, for advice
options.then: Relatives flood the group with opinions, and Zoya is mortified.

options.text: The app's report button, and leave it to the app
options.then: The app thanks you for the report, and you hear nothing back.

options.text: Cybercrime 1930, with the screenshots ready
options.then: The call is taken, and you're asked for the account details and dates.

steps.why: Cybercrime 1930 is the route for online abuse, and saved proof makes it count.

steps.prompt: A week later Zoya jumps whenever her phone buzzes. What do you do?

options.text: Take her phone away for good so this can never happen to her again
options.then: Zoya feels punished for something someone else did.

options.text: Tell her it's all over now, so she can relax

options.text: "Maybe, but I have a bad feeling about it."
options.then: Nikhil rolls his eyes. "That's not a reason."

steps.why: An online profile, or an ID, can't prove who is really typing.

steps.prompt: Nikhil asks: "So what would it take for me to meet him?"

options.text: "Never. Online friends aren't real friends."
options.then: "That's not true," he snaps. "They're my actual friends."

options.text: "Go, then. Just share your live location with me."
options.then: "Deal," Nikhil says, already texting the friend.

options.text: "Take your little cousin along, and then you can go."
options.then: "Okay," he says. "Chintu will love the mall."

options.text: "Not alone. If he's genuine, he won't mind me coming."
options.then: Nikhil thinks. "He might mind, actually."

steps.why: A genuine friend won't mind an adult nearby. One who objects is a flag.

scenarios.relearn: Refusing an online-only meet calmly, without anger or blame, keeps a child safe and still willing to talk to you.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Farah has found an adult pestering her daughter Inaya online, and she's frantic.
scenarios.setup: She's come over with Inaya's phone in her hand.

steps.prompt: Farah says: "I'm taking this phone, and she's never going online again."

options.text: "Good. A year off the phone will teach her."
options.then: "A year at least," Farah says, and wipes the chats.

options.text: "Why was Inaya even talking to a grown man?"
options.then: Farah bristles. "She's thirteen. He tricked her."

options.text: "Take it for now, and see how she's doing tomorrow."
options.then: Farah nods. "I'll switch it off and put it away."

options.text: "Wait. Keep the phone safe. The messages are proof."
options.then: Farah stops. "Proof? I just wanted it gone."

steps.why: Keeping the phone intact keeps the proof a report needs.

steps.prompt: Farah asks: "Inaya won't stop crying. Is this my fault for giving her a phone?"

options.text: "Maybe a bit. Thirteen is young for a phone."
options.then: Farah looks crushed. "I knew it."

options.text: "Don't dwell on it. Just move on, and the whole thing will fade."
options.then: Farah nods, unconvinced. "If only I could."

options.text: "Buy her something nice. It'll cheer her up."
options.then: "She won't want a present," Farah says quietly.

options.text: "No. And it's not Inaya's fault either. Tell her that tonight."
options.then: Farah's eyes fill. "She needs to hear it. So do I."

steps.why: The fault is the adult who targeted her, and both of them need to hear it.

steps.prompt: Farah asks: "Should I go to the police, or is that too much?"

options.text: "Too much. You'll get dragged into a big case."
options.then: Farah hesitates. "So we just let him go?"

options.text: "Find his profile and name and shame him online."
options.then: Farah frowns. "What if he comes after Inaya?"

options.text: "Report his profile on the app. That should be enough."
options.then: "Okay," Farah says. "The app will deal with him?"

options.text: "It's not too much. Report it to cybercrime 1930."
options.then: Farah takes out her phone. "Stay with me while I call?"

steps.why: Cybercrime 1930 is the route for online abuse, and reporting protects other children too.

scenarios.relearn: Steadying a friend toward reassurance, evidence and reporting protects the child better than a panicked over-reaction.

scenarios.hook: Your son Ayaan, 9, mentions an online friend who keeps asking him to keep their chats secret.
scenarios.setup: He says it casually while you drive him home.

steps.prompt: Ayaan says: "He says it's our special thing. Is that okay?"

options.text: "If he wants it secret, that's your business, not mine."
options.then: "Okay," Ayaan says, and looks out of the window.

options.text: "Why are you chatting with strangers at all, Ayaan?"
options.then: Ayaan goes quiet. "He's not a stranger. He plays with me."

options.text: "That's a bit odd. Just stop playing with him, then."
options.then: "But he's my best teammate," Ayaan says, confused.

options.text: "Secret chats are a worry. I'm really glad you told me."
options.then: Ayaan looks surprised. "He said you'd be angry."

steps.why: Naming secrecy as a worry, calmly, teaches him to spot it.

steps.prompt: Ayaan asks: "How do I know if a secret is okay to keep?"

options.text: "All secrets are bad. Tell me every single thing."
options.then: "Every single thing?" Ayaan asks, alarmed.

options.text: "Keep secrets only with grown-ups you know well."
options.then: Ayaan frowns. "But he feels like someone I know."

options.text: "Surprises are fine. No one should ask you to hide things from me."
options.then: Ayaan thinks. "So a birthday surprise is okay?"

options.text: "If a secret ever makes you feel bad inside, then it's a bad secret."
options.then: Ayaan shrugs. "This one feels nice, though."

steps.why: 'No secrets from me' works even when a secret feels nice.

steps.prompt: At home, Ayaan asks: "Do I have to show you the chats?"

options.text: "Yes. Hand the tablet over to me right now."
options.then: Ayaan hands it over, eyes on the floor, and says nothing more.

options.text: "Let's look together. You're not in trouble, whatever's there."
options.then: Ayaan hands you the tablet. "He sent me game coins too."

options.text: "No. I trust you to handle it on your own."
options.then: "Okay," Ayaan says, and runs off to play.

options.text: "I'll check them myself tonight, after you've gone to sleep."
options.then: "Okay," Ayaan says, looking unsure what you'll find.

steps.why: Looking together, with no trouble, keeps him on your side and shows you the full picture.

steps.prompt: At bedtime, Ayaan asks: "What happens to my game friend now?"

options.text: "We'll save his chats together and report him to cybercrime 1930."
options.then: Ayaan nods slowly. "Okay. I'm glad I told you."

options.text: "Nothing. Just block him, and we'll forget all about it."
options.then: "Okay," Ayaan says. "But he plays lots of other games too."

options.text: "I'll message him myself tonight and tell him to get lost."
options.then: Ayaan looks worried. "Then he'll know I told."

options.text: "Let's wait and see if he messages you again before we do anything."
options.then: "Okay," Ayaan says, and pulls up his blanket.

steps.why: Saving and reporting to 1930 protects him and other children, and none of it is his fault.

scenarios.relearn: Naming secrecy as a flag while promising no trouble teaches a child to spot grooming and keep telling you.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Pihu, 15, confesses she sent a photo to someone online, and she's terrified of your reaction.
scenarios.setup: She's sitting on the stairs, not meeting your eyes.

steps.prompt: Pihu whispers: "Are you going to hate me now?"

options.text: "You've shamed this family. I can't even look at you."
options.then: Pihu pulls her knees in. "I'm sorry. I'm so sorry."

options.text: "I'm not angry, Pihu. I'm just very disappointed."
options.then: Pihu's face crumples. "That's worse."

options.text: "Let's not panic. First, what exactly did you send?"
options.then: Pihu goes red. "I can't say it."

options.text: "No. I'm glad you told me, and it's not your fault."
options.then: Pihu looks up, tears spilling. "I thought you'd shout."

steps.why: Lifting the fear first lets her tell you what she needs help with.

steps.prompt: Pihu says: "He's asking for more now, or he'll show my friends."

options.text: "Delete your account tonight. Then he can't reach you."
options.then: "But he already has my friends' names," she says.

options.text: "Don't reply. We'll save the chats and report to cybercrime 1930."
options.then: Pihu nods slowly. "Will they believe me?"

options.text: "Give me the phone. I'll threaten him myself."
options.then: Pihu hesitates. "He said he'd post it if anyone else replied."

options.text: "Block him, and tell your friends to ignore anything he sends them."
options.then: "Then everyone will ask why," she says, panicking.

steps.why: Saving the chats and reporting to 1930 puts the threat with people who can act.

steps.prompt: Pihu asks: "Will I ever stop feeling this stupid?"

options.text: "You'll learn from it. That's what matters now."
options.then: "So I did mess up," Pihu says quietly.

options.text: "You were tricked on purpose. You're not stupid."
options.then: Pihu leans into you. "I just want it to be over."

options.text: "Let's just forget this ever happened, okay?"
options.then: "I can't forget it," she says.

options.text: "Everyone makes mistakes. Don't be so hard on yourself."
options.then: Pihu sighs. "But I still did it."

steps.why: Naming the trickster as the one at fault is what lifts her shame.

scenarios.relearn: Leading with 'glad you told me, not your fault, together' turns a frightened confession into a problem you can handle.

scenarios.source: open door despite not knowing apps
scenarios.hook: You don't know most of the apps your son Raju, 12, uses. You still want him to come to you.
scenarios.setup: He's on the phone while you cook dinner.

steps.prompt: Raju laughs: "Amma, you won't understand. It's a game thing."

options.text: "Maybe not. But if anything online scares you, come to me."
options.then: Raju looks up. "Even if you don't get the app?"

options.text: "Then don't bother bringing any of it to me."
options.then: Raju shrugs. "I wasn't going to."

options.text: "Those games are rubbish anyway. Put the phone away and eat."
options.then: Raju sighs and puts it down. "You always say that."

options.text: "Your didi knows these things better. Ask her."
options.then: "Okay," Raju says. "Didi's always busy, though."

steps.why: You don't need to know the app to be his safe adult. You need the open door.

steps.prompt: Raju asks: "What if someone in the game says something weird?"

options.text: "Show me. We'll sort it out together. No trouble."
options.then: "Okay," he says. "There's one boy who asks lots of questions."

options.text: "Then stop playing that game. Simple as that."
options.then: "But all my friends play it," Raju says.

options.text: "Ignore it. People on phones say strange things."
options.then: "Okay," Raju says, and goes back to his game.

options.text: "Tell your teacher. She knows all about phones and games."
options.then: Raju frowns. "I don't want to tell Ma'am."

steps.why: Promising help and no trouble is what makes him bring it to you.

steps.prompt: A week later, Raju says: "A boy in my game asked where I live. I didn't answer."

options.text: "See? I told you from the very start that this game was trouble."
options.then: Raju's face closes. "Forget it."

options.text: "Good. Now just ignore him, and he'll go away."
options.then: "Okay," Raju says. "He's messaged three times today."

options.text: "Block him, and never tell anyone where you live."
options.then: "I know," Raju says. "I already didn't."

options.text: "Thank you for telling me. Show me, and we'll save it together."
options.then: Raju holds out the phone. "It's here. See?"

steps.why: Thanking him and saving the message keeps him telling you, even when the app is new to you.

scenarios.relearn: You don't need to master every app; promising to always help makes a child bring online trouble to you.

Scolding their new bed-wetting as naughtiness
Comforting them when they seem withdrawn
Keeping the door open so they can tell you

scenarios.why: Forcing feared contact and scolding regression ignore the signs; closeness and comfort honour them.
scenarios.relearn: Forcing feared contact and scolding regression ignore the signs; closeness and an open door honour them.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two lines that tip vigilance into paranoia.

scene.text: "I'll never let my child near any adult again"
"I'll learn the red flags and stay gently alert"
"Every relative is a suspect till proven safe"
"I'll trust my child's discomfort with someone"
"I can stay warm and watchful at once"

scenarios.why: Cutting off all adults or suspecting everyone is paranoia; learning flags is calm vigilance.
scenarios.relearn: Cutting off all adults or suspecting everyone is paranoia; learning flags and staying warm is vigilance.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two 'secret' moves that are red flags.

scene.text: "Don't tell your parents, it's our secret"
"Let's surprise Mum on Sunday"
"This stays between us or you'll be in trouble"
"You can always tell your parents anything"
"We'll surprise the family with cake later"

scenarios.why: Secrets a child must hide from you, especially with threats, are red flags; happy surprises are fine.
scenarios.relearn: Secrets a child must hide from you are red flags; happy surprises everyone soon shares are fine.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two beliefs that would blind you to harm.

scene.text: "It can't happen in a family like ours"
"Harm can reach any child, so I'll stay ready"
"If it were real, there'd be marks to see"
"Many signs show in behaviour, not the body"
"A sudden change is worth a gentle check-in"

scenarios.why: 'It can't happen here' and 'there'd be marks' are myths that blind a parent; readiness keeps you alert.
scenarios.relearn: 'It can't happen here' and 'there'd be marks' blind a parent; readiness and watching behaviour keep you alert.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two things that override your child's body.

scene.text: Forcing a kiss for an uncle 'to be polite'
Letting your child offer a wave instead
Shaming them for not wanting to sit on a lap
Believing them when they shy away
Letting your child decide who hugs them

scenarios.why: Forcing a kiss and shaming override a child's body; a wave, belief and choice protect it.
scenarios.relearn: Forcing affection and shaming override a child's body; a wave, belief and choice protect it.

scenarios.hook: Ramesh chacha keeps taking your daughter Guddi, 8, off alone, with sweets and 'our little secret'.

steps.prompt: He calls Guddi to come for a walk with him again. What do you do?

options.text: Let her go. He's family, so it's rude to think twice
options.then: Guddi goes with him and comes back with a new toy she won't talk about.

options.text: Tell him to his face that you don't trust him
options.then: Ramesh acts deeply hurt, and the family turns on you.

options.text: Say you'll all go together, and stay close
options.then: Ramesh hesitates, then says maybe another day.

options.text: Let her go, but tell her to come straight back
options.then: Guddi returns quickly, and the walks alone carry on each week.

steps.why: Joining in closes off the alone time without an accusation.

steps.prompt: Guddi shows you a new bangle and says it's a secret from chacha. What do you say?

options.text: Give it back. We don't take gifts from anyone
options.then: Guddi cries and hides the bangle under her pillow.

options.text: How lovely. Chacha really spoils you, doesn't he?
options.then: Guddi beams, and the secret stays a secret.

options.text: It's pretty. But no one should ask you to keep secrets from me
options.then: Guddi nods and says chacha told her you'd be cross.

options.text: Ask her, gently, what else chacha has told her to hide from you
options.then: Guddi goes quiet and says she's not allowed to say.

steps.why: A calm no-secrets rule takes away a grooming tool without scaring her.

steps.prompt: At a family lunch, Ramesh offers to have Guddi stay at his place overnight. What do you say?

options.text: Yes. It'll give me a break for a night
options.then: Guddi packs her bag slowly, not looking at you.

options.text: No, she sleeps at home. You're welcome here anytime
options.then: Ramesh shrugs, and the talk moves on.

options.text: Only if her older brother can go along and stay with her
options.then: Ramesh agrees at once, and your unease stays.

options.text: Never. I know exactly what you're up to
options.then: The table falls silent, and Ramesh storms out, calling you mad.

steps.why: Declining calmly keeps her safe without a scene you can't take back.

steps.prompt: A month on, Guddi seems tense whenever chacha's name comes up. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her chacha loves her and she's being silly
options.then: Guddi stops mentioning him at all.

options.text: Check in gently, and say she can tell you anything
options.then: Guddi sits close and says she's glad she can tell you things.

options.text: Keep watching quietly, and say nothing to her yet
options.then: Guddi stays tense, not knowing you've noticed.

options.text: Ask her again and again what chacha did
options.then: Guddi starts crying and says nothing happened.

steps.why: A gentle check-in and an open door let her tell you at her own pace.

scenarios.debrief: Alone time, gifts and secrets: keep things open and watch, don't dismiss it.
scenarios.relearn: Meet engineered alone time, gifts and secrets by keeping things open and watching calmly.

scenarios.hook: Your son Vihaan, 5, now cries and clings to you whenever Bose uncle from next door visits.

steps.prompt: Bose uncle holds out his arms for a hug. What do you do?

options.text: Make him hug uncle so you don't seem rude
options.then: Vihaan goes rigid in Bose uncle's arms and starts to cry.

options.text: Keep Vihaan with you, and say he can just wave today
options.then: Bose uncle lowers his arms, and Vihaan buries his face in your side.

options.text: Laugh and say Vihaan is going through a shy phase
options.then: Bose uncle laughs too, and reaches for Vihaan again.

options.text: Take Vihaan to his room so the visit goes smoothly
options.then: The visit goes smoothly, and no one asks why Vihaan was so upset.

steps.why: Protecting his 'no' tells Vihaan his fear matters to you.

steps.prompt: After the visit, Vihaan is still clingy at bath time. What do you do?

options.text: Tell him big boys don't cry over visitors
options.then: Vihaan stops crying, and stops talking too.

options.text: Ask him outright whether Bose uncle did something bad to him
options.then: Vihaan shakes his head fast and hides under the towel.

options.text: Say gently you saw he was upset, and ask what's changed
options.then: Vihaan says he doesn't want to go to Bose uncle's house any more.

options.text: Distract him with bubbles and a new bath toy
options.then: Vihaan cheers up for a while, and the question goes unasked.

steps.why: A gentle, open question lets him answer at his own pace.

steps.prompt: Next week Bose uncle offers to keep Vihaan while you run errands. What do you do?

options.text: Say yes. He's been a good neighbour for years
options.then: Vihaan screams as you leave, and you tell yourself he'll settle.

options.text: Say yes, but only for half an hour
options.then: Bose uncle says take your time, and Vihaan clings to the gate as you go.

options.text: Thank him but say no, and take Vihaan with you
options.then: Vihaan grips your hand tight all the way to the shops.

options.text: Tell him off loudly for scaring your child
options.then: Bose uncle looks shocked, and the whole building hears by evening.

steps.why: No alone time with someone your child now fears, however familiar.

scenarios.debrief: A sudden, specific fear of someone familiar is a signal: stay close and ask gently.
scenarios.relearn: Treat a sudden fear of someone familiar as a signal; stay close and ask gently, don't force it.

scenarios.hook: An older 'friend' your son Arjun, 15, met online keeps sending him gifts and asks him to keep it quiet.

steps.prompt: A parcel arrives for Arjun, and he grabs it before you can see. What do you do?

options.text: Snatch it and ban his phone in a rage
options.then: Arjun shouts that you never trust him and locks his door.

options.text: Stay calm and ask, with no trouble, who it's from
options.then: Arjun hesitates, then says it's from a gaming friend in college.

options.text: Let it go. Teenagers need their privacy
options.then: The parcel disappears into his room, and so does the story behind it.

options.text: Open it later on, while he's out at school, to see what it is
options.then: You find expensive earphones and no note, and Arjun has no idea you looked.

steps.why: A calm, no-trouble question keeps him talking instead of hiding.

steps.prompt: Two days later, Arjun lets slip that the friend asked him to keep the gifts from you. What do you say?

options.text: Then send every gift back to him right now
options.then: Arjun says that would look weird, and quietly keeps the next one.

options.text: You're far too old to be fooled by a stranger's presents like this
options.then: Arjun's jaw sets, and he says the friend is the only one who gets him.

options.text: Someone asking you to hide gifts is a worry. Let's look together
options.then: Arjun shrugs, then opens the chat for you.

options.text: Just stop accepting any gifts from him from now on
options.then: Arjun agrees, and the chats carry on as before.

steps.why: Naming secrecy as the flag, without blame, keeps him on your side.

steps.prompt: A week later the friend invites Arjun to his flat to try a new game. What do you do?

options.text: Let him go, since he's nearly grown up
options.then: Arjun packs his controller and says he'll be back by nine.

options.text: Say no, save the chats, and report him to cybercrime 1930
options.then: Arjun sighs, but he watches you save the chats and doesn't argue.

options.text: Message the friend yourself and threaten to go to the police
options.then: The friend deletes his account, and the chats vanish with it.

options.text: Say no, and take away his phone for a month
options.then: Arjun hands it over, furious, and stops telling you anything.

steps.why: Saying no calmly and reporting the pattern to 1930 protects him and keeps the door open.

scenarios.debrief: Secret gifts from an older online 'friend' are a flag: stay calm and keep the door open.
scenarios.relearn: Meet secret gifts from an older online 'friend' with calm closeness and an open door, not rage.

scenarios.hook: The school van driver keeps putting your daughter Munni on his lap, and it makes you uneasy.

steps.prompt: At the bus stop, another mother, Seema, laughs and says he's like that with all the kids. What do you do?

options.text: Thank her, but trust your instinct and act on it
options.then: Seema raises her eyebrows, and you decide to act in the morning.

options.text: Let her talk you out of it, so you don't look paranoid
options.then: You nod along, and push the worry down for the night.

options.text: Argue with Seema until she admits you're right
options.then: Seema gets defensive, and the whole bus stop is watching.

options.text: Ask Seema to keep an eye on Munni for you
options.then: Seema agrees half-heartedly, and nothing changes on the van.

steps.why: Your instinct about your child counts, even when others wave it off.

steps.prompt: Next morning the van pulls up and the driver reaches for Munni. What do you do?

options.text: Say calmly that Munni sits in her own seat from now on
options.then: The driver shrugs and waves Munni to a seat by the window.

options.text: Say nothing, and let this morning go
options.then: Munni climbs onto his lap and glances back at you.

options.text: Pull Munni off the van and shout at him
options.then: Munni bursts into tears, and the other children stare.

options.text: Ask Munni in front of him whether she likes sitting there
options.then: Munni shrugs, unsure what you want her to say.

steps.why: A calm, clear rule removes the contact without an accusation.

steps.prompt: That evening Munni asks why you seem so worried about the van driver. What do you say?

options.text: Because that driver is a bad man
options.then: Munni looks frightened and goes quiet for the rest of the evening.

options.text: Your body is yours. Tell me if anything feels wrong
options.then: Munni thinks, then says she didn't like it much anyway.

options.text: Because I said so. Now eat your dinner
options.then: Munni pouts and asks again at bedtime.

options.text: Because big girls like you should sit in their own seat on the van
options.then: Munni sits up proudly, not knowing she can say no to an adult.

steps.why: Body-safety words and an open door make her safer and more likely to tell you. None of it is Munni's fault.

steps.prompt: A few days later, Munni says the driver takes other children on his lap every day. What do you do?

options.text: Tell the school, and call Childline 1098 if they brush it off
options.then: The principal takes notes, and you keep the 1098 number ready.

options.text: Make sure Munni sits in her own seat. The rest isn't your business
options.then: Munni sits by the window, and the other children stay on his lap.

options.text: Warn the other mothers at the bus stop to watch out
options.then: Seema rolls her eyes, and the gossip reaches the driver by evening.

options.text: Stop sending Munni on the van, and take her to school yourself
options.then: Munni is off the van, and the other children still ride with him.

steps.why: Telling the school, and 1098 if needed, protects every child on that van, not only yours.

scenarios.debrief: When someone dismisses your unease about an adult near your child, trust your instinct.
scenarios.relearn: Trust your protective instinct even when others dismiss it, not your fear of looking paranoid.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Riya's respected cricket coach has started giving her 'special' one-on-one sessions behind closed doors.

steps.prompt: Riya is thrilled he has picked her. What do you do?

options.text: Feel flattered, and let the sessions carry on as they are
options.then: Riya stays late twice a week, and the door stays shut.

options.text: Pull her out of cricket altogether, starting today
options.then: Riya is heartbroken, and the coach phones to ask you to bring her back.

options.text: Ask the coach calmly to keep sessions open and observed
options.then: The coach says no other parent has asked, but agrees to leave the door open.

options.text: Ask Riya to tell you if anything ever feels off
options.then: Riya says of course, and the closed-door sessions carry on.

steps.why: Keeping sessions open removes secret access without accusing anyone.

steps.prompt: A week later the coach says Riya needs private one-on-one time to make the trials. What do you say?

options.text: If it helps her make the trials, that's fine by me
options.then: He smiles, and the next session is behind a closed door.

options.text: I'll be watching you, so be careful
options.then: His smile tightens, and he says he only wants what's best for her.

options.text: Okay, but I'll sit right outside the door each time
options.then: You sit outside every session, and the door stays shut.

options.text: It's our rule: an open door, or a group session
options.then: He sighs and says he'll move her to the group nets.

steps.why: Trials don't need closed doors. An open-door rule for every adult keeps her safe.

steps.prompt: Riya comes home saying coach gave her a new bat and told her not to tell the others. What do you do?

options.text: Let her keep it quietly. She's earned it
options.then: Riya hugs the bat, and the secret stays between her and the coach.

options.text: Make her return it to him and apologise
options.then: Riya is confused, and goes quiet at dinner.

options.text: Thank her, and say no adult should ask her for secrets
options.then: Riya frowns and says coach told her it's because she's special.

options.text: Let her keep it, but tell her to share it with the team
options.then: Riya shares the bat, and nobody talks about the secret part.

steps.why: Gifts plus secrets are a grooming pattern, and never Riya's fault. Thanking her keeps her telling you.

steps.prompt: You hear that another girl has suddenly quit his sessions. What do you do?

options.text: Confront the coach at practice, in front of the other parents and kids
options.then: The coach denies everything loudly, and Riya is mortified.

options.text: Warn the other parents in the WhatsApp group
options.then: The group erupts, and the coach hears about it within the hour.

options.text: Quietly move Riya to another academy
options.then: Riya is away from him, and the other children at the academy aren't.

options.text: Report your concern to Childline 1098 and follow their advice
options.then: The counsellor listens, asks a few questions, and explains the next steps.

steps.why: A pattern like this is for Childline 1098 to assess, not for you to prove.

scenarios.debrief: Closed-door 'special' alone time is a flag whoever it is: keep it open and observed.
scenarios.relearn: Closed-door 'special' alone time is a flag; calmly keep sessions open, however respected the adult.

scenarios.hook: Your son Aditya, 9, was always chatty. For two weeks he has been quiet and withdrawn, and you can't place why.

steps.prompt: He barely touches his dinner again tonight. What do you do?

options.text: Ask him sharply what's going on until he answers
options.then: Aditya's eyes fill, and he says 'nothing' again and again.

options.text: Tell yourself it's just a phase that will pass
options.then: Dinner ends in silence, and Aditya goes to his room.

options.text: Later, sit with him and say you've noticed and you're here
options.then: Aditya shrugs, but he stays sitting next to you.

options.text: Ask his class teacher whether something happened at school
options.then: The teacher says he's quiet in class too, and has no idea why.

steps.why: A warm, low-pressure check-in invites him to open up in his own time.

steps.prompt: Over the next few days Aditya still says nothing is wrong. What do you do?

options.text: Keep the door open with small moments together, no pressure
options.then: On a walk, Aditya mentions he hates going to tuition now.

options.text: Take away his games until he's ready to talk
options.then: Aditya shuts down further and stays in his room.

options.text: Drop it, since he keeps saying he's fine
options.then: He stays quiet, and you stop asking.

options.text: Check his phone and school bag for clues while he's asleep
options.then: You find nothing, and Aditya notices his bag was moved.

steps.why: Small, easy moments together make it easier for a child to speak.

steps.prompt: One evening Aditya says he doesn't want to go to tuition any more. What do you say?

options.text: You have to go. Your exams are coming up
options.then: Aditya nods silently and doesn't eat breakfast.

options.text: Which boy at school is bullying you? Tell me his name right now
options.then: Aditya looks confused and says it's not a boy.

options.text: Okay. We'll find you a new tutor, then
options.then: Aditya looks relieved, and changes the subject before you can ask why.

options.text: You don't have to go tomorrow. Can you tell me what changed?
options.then: Aditya picks at his sleeve and says the tuition sir makes him uncomfortable.

steps.why: Backing his reluctance and asking gently honours the signal.

steps.prompt: At bedtime a few days later, Aditya whispers that tuition sir tells him to keep secrets. What do you do?

options.text: Believe him, say it's not his fault, and call Childline 1098
options.then: Aditya holds your hand while you make the call, and breathes easier.

options.text: Ask him exactly what the tuition sir did, and when it started
options.then: Aditya's face shuts, and he says he doesn't remember.

options.text: Tell him you'll have it out with the tuition sir tomorrow
options.then: Aditya panics and begs you not to tell sir he said anything.

options.text: Keep him home from tuition from now on, and leave it at that
options.then: Aditya is away from the tutor, and the tutor still teaches other children.

steps.why: Believing him, saying it's not his fault and calling 1098 is the response that protects him.

scenarios.debrief: A sudden withdrawal calls for a gentle check-in and an open door, not interrogation.
scenarios.relearn: Meet a sudden withdrawal with a gentle check-in and an open door, not interrogation.

scenarios.hook: Helping your daughter Kavya, 6, change, you notice marks on her arms. She has been upset all week.

steps.prompt: Kavya flinches when she sees you looking. What do you do?

options.text: Gasp and demand to know who did this to her
options.then: Kavya bursts into tears and says she fell down.

options.text: Tell her off for playing too rough with the other kids at day care
options.then: Kavya goes silent and pulls her sleeve down.

options.text: Stay calm, hold her, and say she's safe with you
options.then: Kavya relaxes a little and rests her head on your shoulder.

options.text: Say nothing, and get her dressed quickly
options.then: Kavya seems relieved, and the marks go unmentioned.

steps.why: Staying calm makes you safe to tell. Panic can make her shut down.

steps.prompt: At bedtime, Kavya is still upset. What do you say?

options.text: Tell me exactly how you got every single mark
options.then: Kavya says she doesn't remember and turns away.

options.text: If someone hurt you, you should have come and told me at once
options.then: Kavya starts crying and says sorry.

options.text: Don't worry. Marks like these fade in a few days
options.then: Kavya nods, and the question of how she got them stays closed.

options.text: You can tell me anything, anytime. You won't be in trouble
options.then: Kavya holds your hand and whispers, maybe tomorrow.

steps.why: An open, no-trouble door lets her speak when she's ready.

steps.prompt: The next day the marks are still there, and Kavya won't go to day care. What do you do?

options.text: Send her anyway. She has to learn to go
options.then: Kavya clings to the gate and screams as you leave.

options.text: Confront the day care staff in front of the children
options.then: The staff get defensive, and Kavya is frightened by the shouting.

options.text: Keep her home, and put some cream on the marks
options.then: Kavya has a quiet day at home, and no one else sees the marks.

options.text: Keep her home, and have a doctor look at the marks
options.then: The doctor examines them gently and asks to speak with you alone.

steps.why: Keeping her close and getting the marks checked puts her safety first.

steps.prompt: Days later, you still can't explain the marks or her fear. What do you do next?

options.text: Call Childline 1098, describe what you've seen, and ask what to do
options.then: The person on the line listens calmly and explains the next steps.

options.text: Wait until Kavya is ready to tell you more
options.then: Days pass, and Kavya's fear doesn't.

options.text: Go and question everyone at the day care yourself, one by one
options.then: The staff close ranks, and anyone responsible is now on guard.

options.text: Change her day care, and try to move on
options.then: Kavya settles a little, and the marks are never explained.

steps.why: You don't need proof to ask for help. Childline 1098 can guide you.

scenarios.debrief: Unexplained marks plus distress deserve calm comfort and gentle space, not panic.
scenarios.relearn: Meet unexplained marks plus distress with calm comfort and gentle space, not panic or grilling.

scenarios.hook: At a family wedding, relatives keep telling your shy daughter Chhaya, 5, to 'give a kiss' to everyone.

steps.prompt: Your aunt bends down and taps her cheek, waiting. What do you do?

options.text: Nudge Chhaya forward so your aunt isn't offended
options.then: Chhaya kisses her stiffly, then wipes her mouth.

options.text: Say Chhaya is just being difficult today
options.then: Your aunt tuts, and Chhaya hides behind your sari.

options.text: Step in and offer a wave or a high-five instead
options.then: Chhaya waves shyly, and your aunt laughs and waves back.

options.text: Pick Chhaya up and walk away without a word
options.then: Your aunt is left puzzled, and Chhaya never hears that her 'no' is fine.

steps.why: Offering a wave backs her 'no' while staying polite.

steps.prompt: Your mother-in-law says children must respect elders with a kiss. What do you say?

options.text: She can show respect with a namaste. Her body is her choice
options.then: Your mother-in-law sniffs, but lets it drop.

options.text: You're right. I'll make sure she gives everyone a kiss next time
options.then: She nods, and Chhaya looks up at you, worried.

options.text: Your generation had no idea about any of this
options.then: The table goes quiet, and the rest of the lunch is frosty.

options.text: Sorry, she's just shy with new faces
options.then: Your mother-in-law softens, and treats Chhaya's 'no' as shyness to outgrow.

steps.why: Naming her choice, calmly, protects her without shaming anyone.

steps.prompt: On the way home, Chhaya asks if she was naughty for not kissing. What do you say?

options.text: A little. Next time just do it quickly and it's over
options.then: Chhaya nods, and learns her 'no' is something to get past.

options.text: Don't worry about it. Let's just forget it
options.then: Chhaya shrugs, still unsure whether she did something wrong.

options.text: No. You choose who touches you, and I'll back you
options.then: Chhaya smiles and swings your hand all the way home.

options.text: No, but aunty was sad, so try to be nicer next time
options.then: Chhaya frowns, now feeling responsible for aunty's feelings.

steps.why: Telling her plainly that she chooses teaches her that 'no' counts.

scenarios.debrief: Forced 'give a kiss' moments override a child's body; offer a wave instead.
scenarios.relearn: Don't force affection 'to be polite'; offer a wave and let a child's 'no' stand.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Pinki, 10, has gone quiet since school started again.
scenarios.setup: You're folding clothes together after your work shift.

steps.prompt: Pinki sighs: "Amma, can I go to sleep now?"

options.text: "Why are you being so moody all the time? Stop it."
options.then: Pinki drops the shirt. "I'm not moody."

options.text: "Go, beta. You look tired. We'll finish these tomorrow."
options.then: "Okay," Pinki says, and goes without looking back.

options.text: "First tell me why you've been sulking all week."
options.then: Pinki's face closes. "I'm not sulking."

options.text: "Soon. You've seemed quiet lately. You can tell me anything."
options.then: Pinki pauses mid-fold. "Anything?"

steps.why: A gentle check-in names what you see without making her defend herself.

steps.prompt: The next evening, Pinki asks: "Amma, what if someone says a thing is a secret?"

options.text: "Then keep it. A secret is a secret."
options.then: "Okay," Pinki says, and changes the subject.

options.text: "Who said that to you? Tell me right now."
options.then: Pinki's eyes widen. "Nobody. I was just asking."

options.text: "It depends on the secret. Some are fine to keep and some aren't."
options.then: Pinki looks unsure. "How do I know which?"

options.text: "You can still tell me. No one should make you keep secrets from me."
options.then: Pinki nods slowly. "Even a grown-up?"

steps.why: A clear no-secrets rule lets her tell you without feeling she broke a promise.

steps.prompt: At bedtime, Pinki whispers: "Amma, will I get in trouble if I tell you something?"

options.text: "Only if you've done something wrong yourself."
options.then: Pinki goes still. "Then I'll wait."

options.text: "Just tell me. I'm too tired for guessing games."
options.then: "It's nothing," Pinki says, and turns away.

options.text: "I promise I won't tell anyone else. Not even Papa."
options.then: "Promise?" Pinki asks, holding out her little finger.

options.text: "You won't be in trouble. I'm glad you're talking to me."
options.then: Pinki leans against your arm. "Okay. Tomorrow."

steps.why: Promising no trouble, not secrecy, keeps her safe and talking.

scenarios.relearn: A gentle, no-trouble check-in invites a withdrawn child to open up; impatience makes them retreat further.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Mira, 8, used to love visiting Vinod uncle. Now she begs not to go.
scenarios.setup: You're packing the car for Sunday lunch at his house.

steps.prompt: Mira pleads: "Please don't make me go to Vinod uncle's."

options.text: "Don't be silly. He's your uncle, and we're going."
options.then: Mira climbs in silently. "Can I at least sit with you?"

options.text: "If you come, I'll get you ice cream afterwards."
options.then: Mira hesitates. "Will you stay with me the whole time?"

steps.why: Childline listens and guides you, so you don't have to know it all before calling.

steps.prompt: Your husband says the police will make you tell every detail again and again. What do you say?

options.text: I only share what I know. They guide the rest
options.then: He's quiet for a moment, then asks what you'd tell them.

options.text: You're right. Let's leave it to Ravi's parents
options.then: He nods. You both know Ravi's parents haven't done anything yet.

options.text: Then I'll wait until I know every detail
options.then: He shrugs. Days pass, and you still know only what Ravi said.

options.text: I'll ask Ravi to tell me everything first
options.then: He nods. "Better to be sure." You picture Ravi's face and hesitate.

steps.why: You share what you know and professionals ask the rest. Never question the child yourself.

steps.prompt: A few days on, Ravi's mother says she's too frightened to call anyone. What do you do?

options.text: Offer to sit with her while she calls 1098
options.then: She squeezes your hand and dials, with you beside her.

options.text: Tell her it's her family's business now
options.then: She nods, and goes home with the fear still on her face.

options.text: Tell her to wait until she feels ready
options.then: She looks relieved. Ravi's cousin is at their house again that weekend.

options.text: Give her the number and let her call when she can
options.then: She tucks the paper away. Days pass, and she still hasn't called.

steps.why: Nobody has to report alone. Calling together makes the first step easier.

scenarios.debrief: Start with Childline 1098: they listen and guide; you don't report alone.

scenarios.affirm: You don't need to be certain to report; a genuine, good-faith concern is enough, and trained people assess it.
