scenarios.hook: At a house where you work, little Tara now hides whenever her uncle visits. You call Childline, nervous.
scenarios.setup: You keep your voice low so nobody hears.

steps.prompt: A voice says: "Childline. Hello, I'm listening."

options.text: "I'm worried about a child. What should I do?"
options.then: "Thank you for calling. What have you noticed?"

options.text: "Sorry to bother you. It's probably nothing."
options.then: "You're not bothering us. What's on your mind?"

options.text: "I only clean there. Maybe I shouldn't say anything."
options.then: "Anyone can call. What made you worried?"

options.text: "It's a private family matter. Should I even be calling?"
options.then: "A child's safety isn't only a family matter. What have you noticed?"

steps.why: Saying your worry and asking what to do is all it takes to start. That's what the line is for.

steps.prompt: The counsellor says: "Take your time. Tell me about the child and what you've seen."

options.text: "Tara, a little girl. She hides and goes quiet when her uncle visits."
options.then: "That kind of change is worth taking seriously. We'll act on it."

options.text: "She hides when her uncle comes. Maybe I'm imagining it."
options.then: "You don't need to be sure. That's worth us looking into."

options.text: "Tara, a girl where I work. I keep asking if her uncle touched her."
options.then: "It's better not to keep asking her. Let us help with that."

options.text: "Her family are good people. I don't want to blame anyone."
options.then: "Sharing what you saw isn't blaming. It helps us protect her."

steps.why: Describe what you've seen. A child suddenly afraid of a familiar person is a sign to report.

steps.prompt: After you describe what you've seen, the counsellor asks: "Before we go, is anything worrying you about this?"

options.text: "Yes. Losing my job. Can you help me stay safe?"
options.then: "We'll guide you through each step. You're not alone in this."

options.text: "No, I'm fine. Please just forget I called."
options.then: "We can't forget a child's safety. Can we keep your number?"

options.text: "I'll tell her mother myself, so you can stay out."
options.then: "Telling her may help, but please let us act on it too."

options.text: "I'll keep watching and call back once I'm sure."
options.then: "Please don't wait to be sure. We can take it from here."

steps.why: Naming your fear lets them guide you, so you can keep helping Tara.

scenarios.relearn: Open a report by stating your worry and asking for advice; that's what the line is for.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Sunita told you her uncle hurt her. Your mother-in-law has found out you plan to report it.
scenarios.setup: She corners you in the kitchen that night.

steps.prompt: Your mother-in-law says: "Keep quiet, for the family's sake. Think of our name."

options.text: "Sunita comes first. I'm going to report this."
options.then: "You'll destroy this family," she hisses, "over a child's story."

options.text: "Fine. We can keep it between us for now."
options.then: She nods, satisfied. "Good. I'll talk to him myself."

options.text: "I'll think about it after the wedding season."
options.then: "Good. Nobody needs to know till then."

options.text: "Maybe you can just make him apologise to her instead."
options.then: "Yes, yes. I'll make him say sorry. That will be enough."

steps.why: Abuse is a crime. Putting Sunita's safety first, and reporting, is what protects her.

steps.prompt: Next morning she says: "I spoke to him. He swears Sunita imagined it."

options.text: "I believe her. It's not her fault, and she isn't lying."
options.then: She falls silent, her mouth tight.

options.text: "Then I'll sit her down and ask again, in detail."
options.then: "Yes. Ask her properly. You'll see it's nothing."

options.text: "Maybe she misunderstood something he did."
options.then: "Exactly. She's only a child. What does she know?"

options.text: "I don't know. I'll wait and watch him for a while."
options.then: "Good. Waiting is wiser than shouting."

steps.why: Children very rarely lie about abuse. Believe her, and tell her it's not her fault.

steps.prompt: She says: "If you report him, don't expect this family to stand by you."

options.text: "Then I'll stand by Sunita. I'm calling 1098 today."
options.then: She turns away. "Do what you want, then."

options.text: "Please don't say that. I'll do whatever you all decide."
options.then: "Good. Then let this end here, tonight."

options.text: "Then let the elders decide what's fair."
options.then: "Yes. The elders will know how to keep it quiet."

options.text: "Then I'll tell the whole street what he did."
options.then: "Go on," she says coldly. "See who believes you."

steps.why: Sunita's safety comes before the family's approval. Childline 1098 can guide you.

scenarios.relearn: You can name the child's safety as the priority and report, even under family pressure.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Ishita, 14, bursts into tears. Someone online is threatening to leak a photo she sent.
scenarios.setup: She holds out her phone with shaking hands.

steps.prompt: Ishita sobs: "I'm so stupid. Please don't be angry."

options.text: "I'm not angry. It isn't your fault. I'm glad you told me."
options.then: She cries harder, then leans into you. "He says he'll send it to everyone."

options.text: "How could you send that to him? Now look what's happened."
options.then: She pulls the phone back. "I knew you'd say that."

options.text: "Don't cry. We'll delete everything and forget it."
options.then: She wipes her face. "But he still has it."

options.text: "First tell me exactly what you sent, and when."
options.then: She freezes. "Do I have to?"

steps.why: It's never a child's fault when someone threatens them online. Saying so keeps her talking.

steps.prompt: Ishita says: "He wants money by tonight, or he'll post it."

options.text: "We won't pay. Let's save his threats and username."
options.then: She nods, and you screenshot his threats together.

options.text: "Just pay him this once. Then it's over."
options.then: "What if he asks for more?" she whispers.

options.text: "Block him right now and delete the app."
options.then: She blocks him. The chat and his username vanish with the app.

options.text: "Let me message him from your phone and scare him off."
options.then: She hesitates. "What if it makes him angrier?"

steps.why: Saving the evidence, without paying or replying, is what makes a report work.

steps.prompt: Ishita asks: "Do we have to tell anyone? Everyone will know."

options.text: "We'll report it to cybercrime 1930, together."
options.then: She takes a breath. "Okay. Can you do the talking?"

options.text: "No. We'll keep it between us and hope he stops."
options.then: She looks relieved, but her phone buzzes again.

options.text: "Only if he actually posts it. Let's wait and see."
options.then: "Okay," she says, jumping at every notification.

options.text: "Yes, and your phone is gone until you learn."
options.then: She goes silent and hands you the phone.

steps.why: Reporting to cybercrime 1930 together gets help to stop him and shows her she isn't to blame.

scenarios.relearn: Telling a sextorted child it isn't their fault and you'll report together keeps them safe.

scenarios.hook: Your neighbour's son Arnav, 8, has started flinching around his new tutor. You want to call 1098.
scenarios.setup: Your husband Rohan looks up from his laptop.

steps.prompt: Rohan asks: "Aren't you overreacting? You have no proof."

options.text: "A concern is enough to call about. I don't need proof."
options.then: He frowns. "Okay. But what exactly would you say?"

options.text: "Maybe you're right. I'll wait until I'm completely certain."
options.then: He nods and turns back to his screen.

options.text: "I'll ask Arnav a few questions first, to be sure."
options.then: "Would he even tell you?" Rohan asks.

options.text: "I'll mention it to his mother and leave it there."
options.then: "That seems enough," he says. "It's her child."

steps.why: You don't need proof to call. Childline helps work out what's happening.

steps.prompt: A moment later, Rohan adds: "If you do call, that tutor could lose his job."

options.text: "They'll check it fairly. Arnav comes first."
options.then: Rohan is quiet for a moment. "Okay. Arnav first."

options.text: "True. I'd hate to ruin someone's whole life over a hunch."
options.then: "Exactly," he says. "Let it go."

options.text: "He does seem decent. You're probably right."
options.then: He nods. "Teachers get blamed for everything these days."

options.text: "I'll just keep an eye on Arnav for a few more weeks."
options.then: "Good idea," he says. "No harm in waiting."

steps.why: Professionals check a concern fairly. Seeming decent isn't proof of safety, and silence can leave Arnav at risk.

steps.prompt: Later that evening, Rohan asks: "If you call, what if they ask things you don't know?"

options.text: "I'll tell them what I've seen. They'll guide the rest."
options.then: He hands you your phone. "Want me to sit with you?"

options.text: "Then I'll hang up. I don't want to get it wrong."
options.then: "Maybe that's safer," he says with a shrug.

options.text: "Then I'll gently find out more from Arnav before I call."
options.then: "Just don't scare him," Rohan says.

options.text: "Then you call instead. You explain things better."
options.then: "Me? I haven't even seen him," he says.

steps.why: Share what you've seen and let Childline guide you. Never question the child for details.

scenarios.relearn: Reminding yourself a concern is enough, and proof isn't required, helps you act.

scenarios.hook: Nisha, 10, from your building told you the society secretary, Mr Kapoor, hurt her. You plan to report it.
scenarios.setup: At the society meeting, a neighbour pulls you aside.

steps.prompt: Mrs Iyer says: "He's so respectable. Surely the police needn't be involved?"

options.text: "A crime against a child is a crime, whoever did it."
options.then: She stiffens. "But he's done so much for this building."

options.text: "You're right. Someone like him wouldn't do that."
options.then: She smiles, relieved. "I knew you'd see sense."

options.text: "Maybe the committee can deal with it quietly."
options.then: "Yes. Let the committee handle it. No police."

options.text: "I'll wait and see if any other children say anything."
options.then: "Good. One child's story is hardly enough," she says.

steps.why: Respectability isn't safety. A crime against a child needs reporting, whoever did it.

steps.prompt: Mrs Iyer says: "Think of his family. The shame will destroy them."

options.text: "I'm thinking of Nisha. Her safety comes first."
options.then: She looks away and doesn't answer.

options.text: "You're right. I don't want to hurt his family."
options.then: "Exactly. Let it be," she says, patting your arm.

options.text: "Then let's ask him to step down quietly instead."
options.then: "Yes, he can resign. That's more than enough."

options.text: "His family should be ashamed. He deserves all of it."
options.then: She gasps. "You want a public spectacle?"

steps.why: Nisha isn't to blame, and her safety comes before the abuser's family's comfort.

steps.prompt: As you leave, Mrs Iyer asks: "Whatever you decide, can it wait till after the festival?"

options.text: "No. I'm calling Childline 1098 today."
options.then: She sighs. "Then be careful who you tell."

options.text: "Fine. A few more weeks won't matter much."
options.then: "Thank you. It's better for everyone."

options.text: "I'll wait, but I'll keep Nisha away from him."
options.then: "Yes, that's sensible," she says, nodding.

options.text: "I'll post about him in the society group first."
options.then: "You'll start a war in this building," she warns.

steps.why: Report without delay. Waiting can leave Nisha, and other children, at risk.

scenarios.relearn: A child's protection doesn't bend to an abuser's good reputation; report regardless.

scenarios.hook: Your son Raju, 9, told you the shopkeeper at the corner hurt him. Now he watches you nervously.
scenarios.setup: He sits beside you on the mat that evening.

steps.prompt: Raju asks: "Am I in trouble for telling?"

options.text: "No. You're not in any trouble. You did well to tell me."
options.then: He lets out a breath. "He said you'd be angry with me."

options.text: "Not if you promise never to go near that shop again."
options.then: Raju nods quickly. "I promise. I'm sorry."

options.text: "Let's not tell anyone else, and see what happens."
options.then: He looks confused. "So it's a secret now?"

options.text: "You should have come and told me about it the first time."
options.then: His eyes fill with tears. "I was scared."

steps.why: Telling him clearly he's not in trouble keeps him open. It was never his fault.

steps.prompt: Raju whispers: "He said if I told, he'd hurt you."

options.text: "That was a lie to scare you. I'll keep us both safe."
options.then: Raju grips your hand. "Really? You promise?"

options.text: "What else did he say to you? Tell me everything."
options.then: Raju shrinks back and says nothing more.

options.text: "I'll go and shout at him right now, then."
options.then: Raju grabs your arm. "No! Don't go!"

options.text: "Don't worry. We just won't go to that shop ever again."
options.then: He nods, but keeps looking at the door.

steps.why: Threats keep children silent. Calm reassurance, without questions, helps him feel safe.

steps.prompt: Raju asks: "What happens now?"

options.text: "I'll call 1098 for help, and stay with you."
options.then: He leans against you. "Will you stay when they come?"

options.text: "Nothing. We'll forget it ever happened."
options.then: He looks at the floor. "Okay."

options.text: "Your father will sort that man out."
options.then: Raju goes stiff. "Will Papa be angry?"

options.text: "I'll handle it myself. You don't need to know any more."
options.then: He looks unsure. "But what will you do?"

steps.why: Telling him honestly that help is coming, and you'll be there, keeps him safe and calm.

scenarios.relearn: Telling a child they're not in trouble and you'll keep them safe lets them stay open.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Sameer's daughter told him their driver hurt her. He is shaking with anger.
scenarios.setup: He turns up at your door, keys in hand.

steps.prompt: Sameer says: "Come with me. We'll make him confess tonight."

options.text: "Let's not tip him off. We report it to the police."
options.then: Sameer paces. "So we just let him walk around?"

options.text: "Okay. Let's go and have it out with him."
options.then: Sameer turns for the car. "Let's go before I change my mind."

options.text: "Just fire him and never let him near her again."
options.then: "That's it? He just goes to work for another family?"

options.text: "Let's ask her a few more questions first, to be sure."
options.then: "She's already said it once," Sameer snaps.

steps.why: Confronting him can warn him and put the child at risk. Reporting lets professionals act.

steps.prompt: After a call from his wife, Sameer says: "She wants the police. They'll take forever. I want him punished now."

options.text: "Call 1098 with me now, and keep her close tonight."
options.then: Sameer sits down heavily and takes out his phone.

options.text: "Then let's go and scare him ourselves."
options.then: Sameer heads for the door, then stops. "Who stays with her tonight?"

options.text: "Let's wait till morning when we've both calmed down."
options.then: "And tonight? He sleeps in the quarters downstairs."

options.text: "Let's warn the other families he's worked for."
options.then: "Fine, but that doesn't stop him tonight."

steps.why: Reporting now, and keeping her close, protects her better than revenge.

steps.prompt: Sameer's voice breaks as he asks: "What do I even say to her now?"

options.text: "That you believe her and it's not her fault."
options.then: Sameer wipes his eyes. "I can say that."

options.text: "Nothing. Don't bring it up unless she does."
options.then: "Okay," he says, unsure.

options.text: "Ask her gently to tell you exactly what happened."
options.then: "She'll hate that," he says quietly.

options.text: "Tell her you'll make him pay for this."
options.then: "She'll think I'm about to do something crazy."

steps.why: Believe her and say it's not her fault. That's what she needs to hear first.

scenarios.relearn: Reporting rather than confronting keeps evidence intact and the child safer.

Keeping the messages as evidence

scenarios.hook: While you comb her hair, your daughter Lata mentions her uncle's 'special game', then goes quiet.

steps.prompt: Your heart is pounding. What is your first move?

options.text: Stay calm, and say she can tell you at her own pace
options.then: Lata plays with the comb. After a while she says, "He said it's our secret."

options.text: Ask right away what the game is and when he plays it
options.then: Lata's eyes dart away. "Nothing," she mutters.

options.text: Gasp and ask what he did to her
options.then: Lata starts to cry. "Sorry, Amma. I'm sorry."

options.text: Tell her firmly not to play silly games with grown-ups
options.then: She nods and slips out of the room.

steps.why: Calm, open words let her talk at her own pace. Questions or shock can make her shut down.

steps.prompt: Later that evening, Lata whispers that the game makes her feel yucky inside. What do you say?

options.text: Say you believe her, and it's not her fault
options.then: Lata hugs you tight and doesn't let go for a long time.

options.text: Ask if she's sure, since her uncle loves her so much
options.then: Lata lets go of your hand and turns to the wall.

options.text: Ask why she didn't tell you before
options.then: Lata's face crumples. "He said you'd be angry."

options.text: Promise to keep it just between the two of you
options.then: She nods, relieved, and asks you not to tell Papa.

steps.why: Believing her and saying it's not her fault is what she needs to hear first.

steps.prompt: Lata asks if she has to go to her uncle's house on Sunday. What do you say?

options.text: Say she'll stay home with you, and you'll keep her safe
options.then: Lata's whole body loosens. She asks if she can sleep in your bed.

options.text: Say yes, but you'll be in the next room the whole time
options.then: Lata nods, but she goes quiet again for the rest of the evening.

options.text: Say yes. You can't upset the family over a game
options.then: Lata looks at you for a long moment, then says nothing.

options.text: Say you'll decide after you talk to her uncle
options.then: Lata's eyes go wide. "Don't tell him I said!"

steps.why: Keeping her away from him is the first protection. She shouldn't have to face him.

steps.prompt: Your husband says the family will never forgive you if this comes out. What do you do?

options.text: Call Childline 1098 and ask how to report it
options.then: A calm voice listens and explains what happens next. You feel less alone.

options.text: Agree to keep it inside the family for now
options.then: He looks relieved. The uncle's Sunday visits carry on as before.

options.text: Talk to the uncle privately and ask him to stop
options.then: He laughs, says the girl imagines things, and is at your door again next week.

options.text: Ask the family elders what should be done
options.then: The elders decide it must never leave the family.

steps.why: Only professionals can stop him. Childline 1098 guides you to protect her and report.

steps.prompt: A month later, Lata asks if you're still sad about what she told you. What do you say?

options.text: Say you're proud she told you, and it was never her fault
options.then: Lata smiles a little. "Can I tell you things again?"

options.text: Say let's not talk about it anymore
options.then: Lata nods and changes the subject. She doesn't raise it again.

options.text: Say you're fine, and she really shouldn't worry about you
options.then: Lata nods, but keeps watching your face for clues.

options.text: Say you just wish it had never happened to your family
options.then: Lata looks down. "Sorry, Amma."

steps.why: Affirming her bravery and blamelessness keeps the door open for anything else.

scenarios.debrief: The disclosure tool is the sequence: believe, stay calm, no blame, don't interrogate, then act.
scenarios.relearn: On a disclosure, run the steps: believe, stay calm, no blame, let her talk at her pace, then act.

scenarios.hook: Your son Aryan, 10, has been withdrawn for two weeks, since your cousin Nikhil came to stay.

steps.prompt: Aryan skips dinner again and goes to his room. What do you do?

options.text: Sit with him and gently ask how he's been feeling
options.then: Aryan shrugs, but lets you stay. After a while, he says he's tired all the time.

options.text: Leave him be. Boys go through phases
options.then: His door stays shut, and the light stays on late into the night.

options.text: Ask him straight out if Nikhil has done something
options.then: Aryan stiffens. "No. Why would you even ask that?"

options.text: Tell him to stop sulking and join the family
options.then: He comes out, eats in silence and goes straight back.

steps.why: A gentle, open check-in lets him share at his own pace, without pressure.

steps.prompt: Over the next few days, Aryan finds reasons to be out whenever Nikhil is home. What do you do?

options.text: Take it as a sign and make sure they're never alone
options.then: You quietly rearrange the evenings. Aryan seems a little lighter.

options.text: Tell Aryan he's being rude to a guest
options.then: Aryan says sorry, and spends even more time in his room.

options.text: Ask Nikhil if he's noticed anything odd about Aryan
options.then: Nikhil laughs and says Aryan is just a moody kid.

options.text: Let Nikhil take Aryan out to cheer him up
options.then: Aryan goes, silent. He comes back and heads straight to bed.

steps.why: Sudden fear of a familiar person is a sign. Limiting alone time is calm vigilance.

steps.prompt: Your wife says Aryan is odd around Nikhil lately, but it can't be anything, since he's family. What do you say?

options.text: Family or not, a change like Aryan's needs attention
options.then: She pauses. "I didn't want to think about it. What do we do?"

options.text: You're right. Family wouldn't do anything like that
options.then: She nods, relieved, and the subject closes.

options.text: Let's ask Aryan every day until he tells us
options.then: She frowns. "Won't that just make him hide more?"

options.text: Let's confront Nikhil tonight and see how he reacts
options.then: She stares. "Accuse your own cousin? Based on what?"

steps.why: A sign isn't proof, but it's a reason to stay alert and keep checking in.

steps.prompt: One evening, Aryan hovers at your door and says he wants to tell you something. What do you do?

options.text: Put your phone down and listen calmly, at his pace
options.then: Aryan sits on the bed. It takes him a while to start, and you wait.

options.text: Say you're busy and ask if it can wait
options.then: He says it's nothing and goes back to his room.

options.text: Ask right away if it's about Nikhil
options.then: He freezes. "Never mind," he says, backing out.

options.text: Say you're sure it's nothing serious, and give him a hug
options.then: He smiles weakly and doesn't say anything more.

steps.why: Stopping to listen calmly, without leading him, keeps the door open.

scenarios.debrief: For a withdrawn or changed child, the tool is a gentle, open check-in, not waiting it out.
scenarios.relearn: A changed or withdrawn child is a signal to check in gently and openly, not to wait it out or interrogate.

scenarios.hook: At tuition pickup, your daughter's classmate Zoya whispers that the tutor touches her in ways that feel unsafe.

steps.prompt: Zoya is staring at the floor, waiting. What do you do?

options.text: Say you believe her and it's not her fault
options.then: Zoya looks up for a second. "Please don't tell him I said."

options.text: Ask if she's sure, since he's taught for years
options.then: Zoya shrinks back. "Maybe I got it wrong."

options.text: Ask her exactly what he does to her
options.then: Zoya goes silent and pulls at her sleeve.

options.text: Promise you'll speak to him and sort it out
options.then: Zoya's eyes go wide. "He'll know I told!"

steps.why: Believe her and say it's not her fault. Being believed is what keeps a child safe.

steps.prompt: Zoya's mother arrives, rushed and on her phone. What do you do?

options.text: Take her aside and calmly tell her what Zoya shared
options.then: Her mother puts the phone down. "She said that? To you?"

options.text: Say nothing. It isn't your family's business
options.then: They leave. Zoya glances back at you from the gate.

options.text: Hint that Zoya seems unhappy at tuition
options.then: Her mother sighs that Zoya hates maths, and hurries off.

options.text: Tell her to stop sending Zoya there, without saying why
options.then: Her mother looks puzzled and a little offended.

steps.why: Her parent needs to know plainly, so Zoya can be kept away from him and protected.

steps.prompt: That night, you wonder about the tutor's other students. What do you do?

options.text: Call Childline 1098 and report what Zoya told you
options.then: The counsellor takes the centre's details and says they will act on it.

options.text: Have a quiet word with the tutor yourself tomorrow
options.then: The tutor nods, thanks you for "the feedback", and carries on teaching.

options.text: Warn the other parents in the WhatsApp group
options.then: The group explodes with questions, and Zoya's name starts going round.

options.text: Take your own daughter out and leave it at that
options.then: Your daughter is out. The other children still go every day.

steps.why: Reporting to Childline 1098 protects Zoya and others. Never settle it privately.

steps.prompt: A few days later, your daughter asks if something is wrong with Zoya. What do you say?

options.text: Say Zoya's okay, and she can tell you anything too
options.then: Your daughter nods. "Even about a teacher?" she asks, and you say yes.

options.text: Tell her everything Zoya told you
options.then: Your daughter's eyes go wide. By the next day, half the class knows.

options.text: Say it's grown-up business and change the subject
options.then: She shrugs, but looks at you strangely for the rest of the drive.

options.text: Warn her never to be alone with any of her teachers again
options.then: She looks frightened and asks if all teachers are bad.

steps.why: Keeping Zoya's privacy while reminding your child your door is open protects them both.

scenarios.debrief: On a disclosure, the tool is to believe, protect and report via Childline 1098, not to handle it quietly.
scenarios.relearn: Believe a disclosing child, keep her safe, and report through Childline 1098; never settle it privately.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Anika, 12, shows you late-night messages from a gaming 'friend' asking for photos.

steps.prompt: Anika looks scared she's in trouble. What do you do first?

options.text: Thank her, and say she's not in trouble
options.then: Anika breathes out. "He said you'd take my phone away."

options.text: Snatch the phone and delete the whole chat
options.then: The chat is gone, with his username. Anika stares at you, shaken.

options.text: Ask why she's chatting with strangers at night
options.then: Anika's face goes red. "I knew I shouldn't have shown you."

options.text: Reply to him yourself, pretending to be her
options.then: He answers within seconds. Now you're in the chat, with no plan.

steps.why: Thanking her and saying she's not in trouble keeps her coming to you.

steps.prompt: The account messages again while you're looking. What do you do?

options.text: Screenshot the chat and his profile first
options.then: You save what's on screen, with the times and his username.

options.text: Block him right away so it stops
options.then: The messages stop. Nothing was saved first.

options.text: Delete the app from her phone for good
options.then: The app is gone, and every message he sent goes with it.

options.text: Message back that you're calling the police
options.then: The account goes quiet, then disappears.

steps.why: Saving the evidence first gives the report what it needs.

steps.prompt: Anika asks what happens to him now. What do you do?

options.text: Report it together to cybercrime 1930
options.then: The report is filed. Anika watches, and asks if other kids get messages like this.

options.text: Tell her he'll lose interest, so there's nothing more to do
options.then: Anika nods. A week later, a new account adds her with a similar name.

options.text: Tell her you'll handle it, and she should forget it
options.then: She shrugs and goes to bed. You never get round to it.

options.text: Post a warning about him in the parents' group
options.then: Parents reply with worried emojis. No one reports him anywhere.

steps.why: Reporting to cybercrime 1930 is how you get help to stop him, for Anika and other children.

steps.prompt: Anika asks if she has to stop gaming with her friends now. What do you say?

options.text: Agree on safer gaming together, not a ban
options.then: Anika helps set her profile to private and adds only friends she knows.

options.text: Ban all games until she's much older
options.then: Anika goes quiet. Weeks later, she's gaming on a friend's phone.

options.text: Let her carry on as before and forget it
options.then: She's back online that night, with the same open profile.

options.text: Check her phone every single night from now on
options.then: She hands it over each night, and stops telling you things.

steps.why: Staying close and agreeing rules, not banning, keeps her talking to you.

scenarios.debrief: For an online threat, stay calm, keep evidence and report to cybercrime 1930; it's never the child's fault.
scenarios.relearn: Online danger: stay calm, keep the evidence, report to cybercrime 1930; a tricked child is a victim, not at fault.

scenarios.hook: Your nephew Dev, 11, told you a family friend hurt him. The elders want to keep the family's name clean.

steps.prompt: The elders call a family meeting and ask everyone to stay silent. What do you do?

options.text: Say Dev's safety comes first, and you'll report it
options.then: Voices rise. Your aunt says you're shaming everyone.

options.text: Stay quiet to keep the peace at home
options.then: The meeting ends quickly. Dev isn't mentioned again.

options.text: Agree, as long as the friend never visits again
options.then: The elders agree. Nobody tells anyone outside the family.

options.text: Suggest Dev may have misunderstood something innocent
options.then: The elders nod, relieved, and move on to other matters.

steps.why: The child's safety comes before the family's image. Reporting protects him.

steps.prompt: Dev's father asks you not to report, saying Dev will be shamed forever. What do you say?

options.text: Dev did nothing wrong. Reporting protects him
options.then: His father sits down slowly. "I just don't want people talking about him."

options.text: Maybe you're right. I'll leave it to you
options.then: He nods, relieved. Days pass, and nothing is done.

options.text: Then let's send Dev to the village for a while
options.then: He likes the idea. Dev is sent away, and the friend still visits.

options.text: Then let's wait until the friend moves away
options.then: He agrees. Nobody knows when that will be.

steps.why: Dev isn't to blame. Reporting is protection, not a betrayal of the family.

steps.prompt: The next morning, Dev's mother quietly asks what reporting would even involve. What do you do?

options.text: Call Childline 1098 with her, and let them guide you
options.then: She holds the phone between you. The counsellor explains it step by step.

options.text: Tell her you don't really know, and leave it there
options.then: She nods, and the question hangs between you.

options.text: Tell her it means police, court and endless trouble
options.then: Her face goes pale. She says maybe the elders are right.

options.text: Say you'll find out everything first, then tell her
options.then: She waits. A week goes by while you read about it online.

steps.why: Childline 1098 explains the steps and guides you, so no one faces it alone.

steps.prompt: Days later, Dev asks if the family is angry with him. What do you say?

options.text: Say it's not his fault, and you're proud he told you
options.then: Dev's shoulders drop. "Really? Even Dadi?"

options.text: Say the grown-ups are upset, but it'll all pass soon
options.then: Dev nods, but stays out of the room when relatives visit.

options.text: Tell him not to talk about it at home
options.then: Dev goes quiet and stops asking questions.

options.text: Say it's best if he tries to forget it happened
options.then: Dev nods. At night, he still can't sleep.

steps.why: Hearing it's not his fault, and that telling was brave, helps him heal.

scenarios.debrief: The first priority is always the child's safety, over the family's image or comfort.
scenarios.relearn: The child's safety comes first, over the family's image; reporting is protective, not a betrayal of the family.

scenarios.hook: Your employer gave you a leaflet on child safety weeks ago. It's still in your bag, unread.

steps.prompt: On the bus home, you find the leaflet under your purse. What do you do?

options.text: Save Childline 1098 and cybercrime 1930 now
options.then: It takes a minute. The numbers sit in your phone, next to your sister's.

options.text: Put it back. You'll deal with it if anything happens
options.then: The leaflet slides back under your purse.

options.text: Throw it away. Reading it only makes you anxious
options.then: It goes in the bin at the bus stop. The worry stays.

options.text: Give it to your husband to keep safe instead
options.then: He puts it in a drawer and forgets about it.

steps.why: Saving the numbers now means help is one tap away if you ever need it.

steps.prompt: That night, you have ten quiet minutes once the children sleep. What do you do?

options.text: Look up the warning signs and read them once
options.then: Some of it is hard to read. You remember: sudden fear of someone familiar, withdrawal, new secrets.

options.text: Watch a serial instead to unwind
options.then: The episode ends. You fall asleep with the TV on.

options.text: Read scary news stories to see what really happens
options.then: You scroll until late, frightened, and learn nothing you can use.

options.text: Plan to look it all up in one go on your day off
options.then: Your day off fills up with chores, as always.

steps.why: Knowing a few key signs helps you notice early and check in calmly.

steps.prompt: Your friend Sarita says reading about abuse will make you suspect everyone. What do you say?

options.text: It's about noticing calmly, not suspecting everyone
options.then: Sarita thinks about it, then asks where she could learn more.

options.text: Maybe. Some things are better not to know
options.then: She agrees, and you both change the subject.

options.text: It's strangers we really need to watch for anyway
options.then: Sarita nods. You both warn your children about strangers that evening.

options.text: I'll only read more if something happens to my children
options.then: She nods. Neither of you opens the subject again.

steps.why: Awareness is calm vigilance, not suspicion. Most harm comes from people a child knows.

scenarios.debrief: Prepare despite the fear: an informed, ready parent is a child's safety when it counts.
scenarios.relearn: Prepare despite the fear; save the numbers and learn the signs now, as crisis is the hardest time to learn.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Mira, 7, has been silent and clingy since a sleepover at her friend Ananya's house.

steps.prompt: At bedtime, Mira won't let go of your hand. What do you do?

options.text: Cuddle up and gently ask how the sleepover felt
options.then: Mira is quiet a long time, then says she didn't like it there.

options.text: Ask about every single hour she was away, one by one
options.then: Mira's answers get shorter. Then she says she's sleepy.

options.text: Tell her she's too big to be so clingy now
options.then: Mira lets go and turns to face the wall.

options.text: Tell her a funny story so she forgets it
options.then: She laughs at the story, then holds your hand again.

steps.why: A warm, no-pressure question lets a worry come out safely.

steps.prompt: Ananya's mother invites Mira for another sleepover this weekend. What do you do?

options.text: Say not this time, and keep checking in with Mira
options.then: Ananya's mother says it's no problem. Mira looks relieved when you tell her.

options.text: Say yes. Mira needs to get over being shy
options.then: On Saturday morning, Mira cries and begs not to go.

options.text: Say yes, and tell Mira to call if anything's wrong
options.then: Mira nods, but won't look at you.

options.text: Ask Ananya's mother what went on that night
options.then: She says the girls had fun, and asks if Mira said something.

steps.why: Respecting her discomfort protects her. Don't push a child back where she feels uneasy.

steps.prompt: A few days later, Mira says Ananya's uncle told her to keep a secret. What do you do?

options.text: Thank her calmly and say she's not in trouble
options.then: Mira hesitates, then whispers, "He said I would be if I told."

options.text: Ask her again and again what the secret was
options.then: Mira clams up. "I promised," she says.

options.text: Tell her some secrets with grown-ups are fine to keep
options.then: Mira nods slowly and changes the subject.

options.text: Phone Ananya's mother right away to complain
options.then: The call turns heated, and Mira hears you shouting.

steps.why: A grown-up asking a child for secrets is a red flag. She's not in trouble, and it's never her fault.

steps.prompt: Mira mentions the secret to her father too. He says the uncle is just being playful. What do you say?

options.text: Say it's a red flag, and you'll call 1098 for advice
options.then: He frowns, then says, "Okay. Put it on speaker. I want to hear."

options.text: Agree it's probably harmless, and let it go for now
options.then: He nods. Mira is invited to Ananya's birthday next week.

options.text: Say you'll ask Mira every day until you're sure
options.then: He shrugs. "If you must."

options.text: Say you'll go and confront the uncle yourself
options.then: He sighs. "And say what, exactly?"

steps.why: Secrets are a grooming red flag. Childline 1098 can advise you on what to do next.

scenarios.debrief: A sudden change is a signal to check in gently, take it seriously, and keep the door open.
scenarios.relearn: Take a sudden change in a child seriously; a gentle, open check-in is the tool, never interrogation or dismissal.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Geeta starts telling you something about the landlord's son, then stops and begs you not to tell anyone.

steps.prompt: Geeta holds your hand tight, waiting for your promise. What do you say?

options.text: Say you'll keep her safe, but can't keep it secret
options.then: Geeta looks scared. "Then who will you tell?"

options.text: Promise you'll never tell a single soul
options.then: Geeta relaxes and tells you a little more. The promise weighs on you.

options.text: Say you won't tell anyone in the family
options.then: Geeta nods slowly, not sure what that means.

options.text: Say you can't promise anything until she tells it all
options.then: Geeta pulls her hand away and goes quiet.

steps.why: Honest reassurance keeps her trust. A secrecy promise you'd have to break would hurt more.

steps.prompt: Geeta says he told her the family would be thrown out if she told. What do you say?

options.text: Say it's not her fault, and you'll keep her safe
options.then: Geeta cries quietly into your shoulder.

options.text: Say you'll need to think it over before you do anything
options.then: Geeta watches your face, trying to read it.

options.text: Say she should just keep away from him for now
options.then: Geeta nods. She stops going to the water tap alone.

options.text: Ask her exactly what he did to her
options.then: Geeta shakes her head and won't say more.

steps.why: Threats keep children silent. Hearing it's not her fault, and she's safe, matters most.

steps.prompt: The next day, you're scared of losing your home if you report. What do you do?

options.text: Call Childline 1098 and ask how to keep you both safe
options.then: The counsellor listens and explains how they can help without you facing him alone.

options.text: Stay quiet. You can't risk the roof over your heads
options.then: Days pass. Geeta flinches whenever there's a knock at the door.

options.text: Tell the landlord what his son did
options.then: The landlord goes red and says you have a week to leave.

options.text: Keep Geeta indoors whenever he's around
options.then: Geeta is safer for now, but no one outside knows.

steps.why: Childline 1098 can guide you on protecting Geeta and keeping your family safe.

steps.prompt: One evening, Geeta asks if she did something wrong by telling. What do you say?

options.text: Say telling was brave, and none of it is her fault
options.then: Geeta leans on you. "Will you stay with me tonight?"

options.text: Say it's done now, so she should forget it
options.then: Geeta nods, but keeps her eyes on the door.

options.text: Say she should have told you the first time
options.then: Geeta's face falls. "I was scared."

options.text: Say it's fine, as long as she doesn't tell anyone else
options.then: Geeta nods, confused, and goes quiet.

steps.why: Hearing she was brave and blameless helps her heal, and keeps her telling you.

scenarios.debrief: Never promise total secrecy; tell her you believe her, that it's not her fault, and that you'll keep her safe.
scenarios.relearn: Never promise total secrecy; tell her you believe her, it's not her fault, and you'll keep her safe, while free to act.

myth.why: Readiness is protection, the same as knowing first aid you hope never to use.

myth.re: A child heals better when you affirm their bravery, their blamelessness, and that your door stays open, than in silence.
myth.why: Silence can feel like shame; steady, open support helps healing.

scenarios.relearn: After reporting, affirm a child's bravery and blamelessness and keep the door open; silence can feel like shame.

scenarios.hook: "My child seems fine, so I can put the whole safe-adult toolkit away."

myth.un: My child seems fine, so I can put the whole safe-adult toolkit away.
myth.re: Stay the tellable, alert, ready adult anyway; the open door and the saved numbers matter at every age, online and off.
myth.why: The safe adult stays the safe adult, not just during a crisis.

scenarios.relearn: Stay tellable, alert and ready even when all seems fine; the open door and the toolkit matter at every age.

scenarios.affirm: Every other tool only works because a child believes they can come to you; that open door is your strongest one.
scenarios.relearn: The open, no-blame door is the tool every other one depends on; being reachable is your strongest protection.

scenarios.relearn: The check-in tool is just sitting close and asking gently how a withdrawn child is, with no pressure.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Pinky, 11, whispers that her coaching teacher makes her feel uncomfortable.
scenarios.setup: She won't look at you as she says it.

steps.prompt: Pinky says: "He keeps asking me to stay back after class."

options.text: "Thank you for telling me. I believe you."
options.then: Pinky finally looks up. "You're not angry?"

options.text: "Are you certain? He's such a respected teacher."
options.then: Pinky looks down. "Maybe I'm wrong."

options.text: "What does he do when you stay back? Tell me."
options.then: Pinky's face closes. "Nothing. Forget it."

options.text: "Just leave early from now on. Problem solved."
options.then: Pinky nods, but her hands are still shaking.

steps.why: Thanking and believing her are the first words that keep her talking.

steps.prompt: Pinky asks: "Did I do something wrong?"

options.text: "No. None of this is your fault."
options.then: She lets out a long breath and leans on you.

options.text: "You should have told me sooner. That's all."
options.then: Pinky's eyes fill. "I was scared to."

options.text: "Maybe don't be so friendly with your teachers."
options.then: She stares at you. "I wasn't being friendly."

options.text: "We'll talk about that later. Go and rest now."
options.then: She stops at the door, still looking unsure.

steps.why: She must hear clearly that none of it is her fault. The blame is his alone.

steps.prompt: Pinky asks: "Do I have to go to coaching tomorrow?"

options.text: "No. I'll keep you safe and call 1098 for help."
options.then: Pinky hugs you tight. "Okay."

options.text: "Yes. We've paid the fees for the whole year."
options.then: Pinky goes very quiet.

options.text: "Yes, but I'll wait right outside the whole time."
options.then: She nods, but doesn't let go of your hand.

options.text: "No. And I'll go and shout at him tomorrow."
options.then: Pinky panics. "Please don't. Everyone will know!"

steps.why: Keeping her away from him and calling 1098 is how you keep your promise to protect her.

steps.prompt: Pinky whispers: "My friend Chinki has to stay back too."

options.text: "I'll tell the helpline, so she's kept safe too."
options.then: Pinky nods. "She doesn't like it either."

options.text: "That's Chinki's mother's problem, not ours."
options.then: Pinky looks worried. "But she's my friend."

options.text: "Tell me everything you've seen happening to her there."
options.then: Pinky shifts uneasily. "I don't know. I just saw."

options.text: "Don't tell anyone else about this, okay?"
options.then: Pinky nods slowly, unsure why.

steps.why: Other children may be at risk. Passing it on to Childline protects them too.

scenarios.relearn: Open a disclosure with belief and reassurance: 'I believe you. It's not your fault. I'll keep you safe.'

scenarios.hook: Your neighbour's son Imran, 8, lingers at your door and says an adult at home hurts him.
scenarios.setup: He looks back over his shoulder as he speaks.

steps.prompt: Imran whispers: "Please don't tell him I said."

options.text: "I believe you. You're not in trouble for telling."
options.then: Imran nods slowly. "He gets really angry."

options.text: "That's a family matter. I shouldn't get involved."
options.then: Imran's face falls. He turns to go, then hesitates.

options.text: "I won't tell anyone. It'll be our secret."
options.then: Imran looks relieved. "Promise?"

options.text: "Who is it? Your father? Your uncle? Tell me."
options.then: Imran backs away. "I have to go."

steps.why: Believe him and say he's not in trouble. Don't promise a secret you can't keep.

steps.prompt: Imran asks: "Are you going to tell my mum?"

options.text: "I'll call people whose job is to keep you safe."
options.then: Imran bites his lip. "Will they be nice?"

options.text: "Yes. I'll go and talk to your family right now."
options.then: Imran grabs your arm. "No, please! He'll know!"

options.text: "No. I'll keep an eye out and see what happens."
options.then: Imran nods, but looks back at his door.

options.text: "No. This stays just between us, okay?"
options.then: Imran nods. "Okay. Our secret."

steps.why: Childline 1098 can protect him safely. Going to the family could put him at more risk.

steps.prompt: Imran asks: "Can I stay here a little while?"

options.text: "Yes. Sit with me while I call Childline 1098."
options.then: He sits close and watches you dial.

options.text: "Better not. Your family will worry. Go home."
options.then: He turns toward his door, then stops and looks back at you.

options.text: "Yes, stay the night. I'll deal with him myself."
options.then: Imran looks scared. "He'll come looking for me."

options.text: "Yes. Now tell me everything, from the start."
options.then: Imran curls up and goes silent.

steps.why: Keeping him with you while you call 1098 keeps him safe right now.

steps.prompt: Imran whispers: "Is it my fault he gets angry?"

options.text: "Never. When a grown-up hurts you, it's not your fault."
options.then: Imran is quiet, then nods. "Okay."

options.text: "Maybe try to stay out of his way when he's angry."
options.then: Imran nods seriously, as if it's his job now.

options.text: "We'll talk about that later. Let's wait for help."
options.then: Imran looks down, still carrying the question.

options.text: "He's the one with the problem. Don't think about it."
options.then: Imran frowns, trying to understand.

steps.why: He needs to hear clearly that it's never his fault, whatever he did or didn't do.

scenarios.relearn: Believe a child who tells you, reassure them they're not in trouble, and route to help via Childline 1098.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Riya, 7, told you both that her uncle Rakesh hurt her. Your wife Kavita grabs her car keys.
scenarios.setup: Riya is in the next room and can hear you.

steps.prompt: Kavita shouts: "I'm going to Rakesh's house to have it out with him!"

options.text: "Wait. Riya can hear us. Let's stay calm for her."
options.then: Kavita stops, keys still in hand. "How can I be calm?"

options.text: "Yes. Let's go over there together, right now."
options.then: Kavita is already at the door. In the next room, Riya starts to cry.

options.text: "Calm down. You're overreacting."
options.then: "Overreacting?" Kavita snaps. "She's our daughter!"

options.text: "Call him instead, and tell him off on the phone."
options.then: Kavita dials. Rakesh doesn't pick up, then texts that it's all lies.

steps.why: Riya is listening. Staying calm keeps her from feeling she caused the storm.

steps.prompt: Kavita stops at the door and says: "He's my own brother. What do we do?"

options.text: "We call Childline 1098 now and keep Riya close."
options.then: Kavita sinks onto the sofa. "Okay. You dial."

options.text: "Maybe we let your parents handle him."
options.then: "They'll tell him off and forget it," she says.

options.text: "Then let's warn him to stay away from her."
options.then: "And he carries on with other kids?" she says.

options.text: "Let's wait until we're sure. She's only seven."
options.then: Kavita stares at you. "She told us, didn't she?"

steps.why: Reporting lets professionals act, without tipping him off or putting Riya at risk.

steps.prompt: Kavita asks: "What do we tell Riya now?"

options.text: "That she's safe, and none of this is her fault."
options.then: Kavita wipes her face. "Let's tell her together."

options.text: "Nothing. We shouldn't upset her any more."
options.then: Kavita hesitates. "She'll think we didn't care."

options.text: "That her uncle will be punished for this."
options.then: "Is that what she needs to hear?" Kavita asks.

options.text: "To tell us exactly what happened, step by step."
options.then: "Won't that scare her?" Kavita asks.

steps.why: She needs to hear she's safe and blameless. Leave the details to professionals.

scenarios.relearn: Don't confront in a rage; keep the child close and calm, and report through Childline 1098 so professionals can act.

scenarios.hook: Your son Aman, 9, has started telling you what happened at his cousin's house. It comes out slowly, in pieces.
scenarios.setup: He's sitting on the edge of his bed.

steps.prompt: Aman says: "It was after dinner. No, before. I don't know."

options.text: "Take your time. I'm here, and I'm listening."
options.then: Aman takes a shaky breath. "It happened more than once."

options.text: "Wait. Start from the beginning, step by step."
options.then: Aman stops. "I can't remember it like that."

options.text: "Before or after? It matters. Think carefully."
options.then: Aman's eyes fill. "I don't know!"

options.text: "It's okay. You don't have to tell me any of it."
options.then: Aman looks relieved, and goes quiet.

steps.why: Letting him talk at his own pace keeps him talking. Details are for professionals.

steps.prompt: Aman says: "I don't want to say the rest."

options.text: "That's okay. You've told me enough to get help."
options.then: Aman nods. "Is that really enough?"

options.text: "You have to. I need every detail to help you."
options.then: Aman shuts his eyes and shakes his head.

options.text: "Just one more thing. Who else was there?"
options.then: Aman pulls his knees up and won't answer.

options.text: "Then let's pretend none of it happened."
options.then: Aman looks at you, unsure what that means.

steps.why: You don't need every detail to act, and none of it is his fault. Leave questions to professionals.

steps.prompt: Aman asks: "What happens now?"

options.text: "I'll keep you safe and call Childline 1098."
options.then: He leans on your shoulder. "Will you stay with me?"

options.text: "Nothing. It's over now, so forget it."
options.then: Aman nods, but doesn't look convinced.

options.text: "I'm going to go over there and deal with this myself."
options.then: Aman grabs your hand. "Please don't leave."

options.text: "We'll see. Let me think about it for a while."
options.then: Aman watches your face, waiting.

steps.why: Saying you'll keep him safe and get help tells him it's in good hands.

scenarios.relearn: Let a child talk at their own pace; listen without interrogating, and leave detailed questioning to professionals.

scenarios.hook: Your youngest, Sonu, 6, has just told you the man next door hurt him. Now he's clutching your sari.
scenarios.setup: His voice is barely a whisper.

steps.prompt: Sonu begs: "Promise you'll never tell anyone. Promise!"

options.text: "I'll always keep you safe. I can't keep this a secret."
options.then: Sonu's lip trembles. "But he said..."

options.text: "I promise. This stays between just us two, forever."
options.then: Sonu nods and wipes his eyes. The secret is yours now too.

options.text: "Okay, okay. I won't tell Papa, at least."
options.then: Sonu nods, but still looks scared.

options.text: "Why? What else are you hiding from me?"
options.then: Sonu flinches. "Nothing!"

options.text: "I'll show him. Just wait till I see him."

options.then: Sonu nods fast. "Yes. Don't tell."

options.text: "Don't worry about me. I can look after myself, beta."

steps.prompt: Later, Sonu asks: "Who else has to know?"

options.text: "People who keep children safe. I'll be with you."
options.then: Sonu holds your hand. "The whole time?"

options.text: "Nobody yet. Let me think about it first."
options.then: Sonu relaxes a little. "Good. Don't tell yet."

options.text: "The whole basti, so everyone knows what he is."
options.then: Sonu goes pale. "Everyone?"

options.text: "Just your father. He'll handle it his way."
options.then: Sonu stiffens. "Papa gets so angry."

steps.why: Telling him honestly who will help, and that you'll be there, keeps his trust.

scenarios.relearn: Never promise total secrecy; reassure that you'll keep the child safe while staying honest that you may need to act.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Farah calls. Her daughter Aliya has just told her an older cousin hurt her.
scenarios.setup: Farah is breathing fast and barely making sense.

steps.prompt: Farah gasps: "I can't think. I just froze when she told me."

options.text: "Breathe. Freezing is normal. You can still help her."
options.then: Farah takes a slow breath. "Okay. Okay. What do I do?"

options.text: "Pretend it's nothing, and maybe it'll blow over."
options.then: "Pretend?" Farah says. "She's crying in her room."

options.text: "You froze? She'll think you didn't believe her."
options.then: Farah starts sobbing. "I've ruined it."

options.text: "Hang up and go and ask her for every single detail."
options.then: "Every detail?" Farah repeats, unsure.

steps.why: Steadying her first helps her go back to her daughter calm.

steps.prompt: Farah asks: "What do I say to Aliya now?"

options.text: "Tell her you believe her and it's not her fault."
options.then: Farah repeats it slowly. "I believe you. It's not your fault."

options.text: "Ask her if she's sure it really happened."
options.then: "She'd hate me for asking that," Farah says.

options.text: "Tell her you'll keep it a secret, just between you two."
options.then: "That would calm her down," Farah says.

options.text: "Tell her you'll make him pay for it."
options.then: "She'll panic about the family," Farah says.

steps.why: Believing her and saying it's not her fault is what she needs to hear first.

steps.prompt: Farah asks: "And then? My family will want to hush it up."

options.text: "Keep her safe. Let's call Childline 1098 together."
options.then: Farah exhales. "Can you stay on the line while I call?"

options.text: "Then hush it up. It's your family's decision."
options.then: "I don't want to," Farah says quietly.

options.text: "Wait a few days until everyone is a bit calmer."
options.then: "And if he visits again?" she asks.

options.text: "Go and confront the cousin tonight."
options.then: "He'll just deny it," Farah says.

steps.why: Keeping her safe and calling 1098 together gets real help, without Farah facing it alone.

steps.prompt: Farah whispers: "I keep thinking I should have seen it."

options.text: "This is on him, not you. You're helping her now."
options.then: Farah is quiet, then says, "Okay. I'm going to her now."

options.text: "Maybe. Be more careful from now on."
options.then: Farah's voice cracks. "I know. I know."

options.text: "Don't think about that. Just move on."
options.then: "I can't just move on," she says.

options.text: "We all miss things. You'll feel better tomorrow."
options.then: "Will I?" Farah asks, still shaky.

steps.why: Blame belongs to the abuser alone. A steady parent helps a child heal.

scenarios.relearn: Guide a panicking parent through the steps: believe, no blame, keep safe, and call Childline 1098 together.

scenarios.hook: Your son Omkar, 13, tells you someone posing as a girl tricked him into sending a photo, and now threatens him.
scenarios.setup: He can't look at you.

steps.prompt: Omkar mutters: "I'm such an idiot. You must hate me."

options.text: "You're not in trouble. This is on him, not you."
options.then: Omkar looks up, surprised. "Really?"

options.text: "Why on earth would you send something like that?"
options.then: Omkar's face goes red. He stares at the floor.

options.text: "It's okay. Everyone makes stupid mistakes."
options.then: Omkar nods miserably. "I know it was stupid."

options.text: "Show me everything you sent, right now."
options.then: Omkar grips his phone tighter.

steps.why: Sextortion is never the child's fault. Saying so plainly lifts the shame.

steps.prompt: Omkar says: "He wants money by tomorrow or he'll send it to my class."

options.text: "We won't pay. Let's screenshot his threats first."
options.then: Omkar hands over the phone. "I didn't delete anything."

options.text: "Let's just pay once and be done with it."
options.then: Omkar hesitates. "What if he asks again?"

options.text: "Delete your account right now."
options.then: Omkar starts deleting. The chats begin to vanish.

options.text: "Block him first. We'll deal with the rest later."
options.then: Omkar blocks him. The messages stop, for now.

steps.why: Keep the evidence and don't pay. Paying rarely stops the threats.

steps.prompt: Omkar asks: "Do we have to tell anyone? Everyone will find out."

options.text: "We'll report it to cybercrime 1930. You're not alone."
options.then: He nods slowly. "Can you do the talking?"

options.text: "No. We'll keep this to ourselves."
options.then: Omkar relaxes, but flinches when his phone buzzes.

options.text: "Only if he actually goes and sends it to your class."
options.then: "So we just wait?" Omkar asks.

options.text: "Yes, and no phone for a year after this."
options.then: Omkar's face falls. He hands you the phone.

steps.why: Reporting to cybercrime 1930, with you beside Omkar, is how you get help to stop the threats.

steps.prompt: A week later, Omkar asks: "Can I still play online with my friends?"

options.text: "Yes. Let's set up your privacy settings together."
options.then: Omkar pulls his chair closer. "Okay. Show me."

options.text: "No. No more online anything, ever."
options.then: Omkar shrugs and goes quiet. Later you see him on a friend's phone.

options.text: "Sure. Just don't be so stupid next time."
options.then: Omkar's face goes red again. "Fine."

options.text: "Only if I can read all of your chats, every single night."
options.then: Omkar sighs. "So you don't trust me now."

steps.why: Staying close and setting things up together, not banning, keeps him coming to you.

scenarios.relearn: A sextorted child is a victim, not at fault; reassure, keep evidence, and report to cybercrime 1930 together.

scenarios.hook: At a family function, your daughter Tanvi told you an older cousin hurt her. Some relatives overheard.

options.text: "Tanvi's safety comes before our comfort."
options.then: Your aunt folds her arms. "And the family's name?"

options.text: "You're right. Let's not make a scene today."
options.then: Your aunt nods. "Sensible. We'll talk later."

options.text: "Fine, as long as he apologises to her."
options.then: "Of course. We'll make him say sorry," she says.

options.text: "I'll decide once the guests have gone home."
options.then: "Good. No need to spoil the day," she says.

options.text: "We believe her. Children rarely make this up."
options.then: The room goes quiet.

options.text: "Maybe. I'll ask her again, more carefully."
options.then: "Yes. Ask her properly," the aunt says.

options.text: "Maybe she did. Let's not jump to conclusions."
options.then: The aunts nod, relieved.

options.text: "How dare you! Get out of this room!"
options.then: The aunt storms out, and the family starts taking sides.

options.then: Nobody speaks. Your uncle turns away.

options.text: "Please, I don't want to lose everyone."
options.then: Your uncle nods. "Then let it be."

options.text: "I'll report it once I've warned his parents."
options.then: "His parents will talk you out of it," he says.

scenarios.relearn: The child's safety comes before the family's comfort; believe, protect, and report rather than hush it up.

scenarios.hook: Your son Neel, 9, has been quiet and off his food for a week. You sit down beside him on the sofa.
scenarios.setup: He keeps his eyes on his cartoon.

steps.prompt: Neel mumbles: "What? I'm watching."

options.text: "You've seemed a bit down lately. I'm here to listen."
options.then: Neel shrugs. "I'm fine." But he turns the volume down.

options.text: "What's wrong with you these days? Out with it."
options.then: Neel turns the volume up. "Nothing."

options.text: "Is someone troubling you? Is it someone at school?"
options.then: Neel stiffens. "No. Why?"

options.text: "Nothing. I just wanted to sit here with you."
options.then: Neel nods and keeps watching.

steps.why: Naming the change gently, and offering to listen, opens the door without pressure.

steps.prompt: Neel says: "I don't want to go to swimming anymore."

options.text: "Okay. What feels different about it now?"
options.then: Neel picks at the sofa. "I just don't like the changing room."

options.text: "You have to. We've paid for the whole term."
options.then: Neel's face shuts. "Fine."

options.text: "Did something happen? Did someone touch you?"
options.then: Neel goes red and gets up, then hovers by the door.

options.text: "No problem. You can quit, no questions asked."
options.then: Neel looks relieved and turns back to the TV.

steps.why: An open question lets him explain in his own words, without leading or pushing.

steps.prompt: Neel whispers: "Can I tell you something if you don't get mad?"

options.text: "You can tell me anything. I won't be mad at you."
options.then: Neel takes a deep breath and moves closer.

options.text: "That depends on what you've done."
options.then: Neel shakes his head, then says quietly, "It's not something I did."

options.text: "Of course. But first, who is it about?"
options.then: Neel hesitates and looks away.

options.text: "I'll try not to get mad, but I can't promise anything."
options.then: Neel looks unsure and stays quiet.

steps.why: Promising calm, not anger, is what makes you the adult he can tell.

steps.prompt: After a pause, Neel says: "The coach makes me change in his office. I don't like it."

options.text: "I'm glad you told me. It's not your fault. I'll get help."
options.then: Neel's shoulders drop. "Do I have to go back there?"

options.text: "Maybe he's just trying to help you get ready faster."
options.then: Neel looks away. "Forget it."

options.text: "What else happens in there? Tell me everything now."
options.then: Neel pulls his knees up and goes silent.

options.text: "I'll go and shout at that coach tomorrow."
options.then: Neel's eyes go wide. "Everyone will know!"

steps.why: Thank him, say it's not his fault and get help. Keep him away, and don't question him.

scenarios.relearn: Open a check-in gently: name the change, offer your presence, and leave the door open with no pressure.

options.text: "Let's just forget it ever happened."

options.text: "I'm not angry. Just very, very tired."
options.then: Rani goes quiet, unsure what that means.

options.then: Rani lets out a long breath. "Really?"

options.text: "Nani means well. Let's not upset her."
options.then: Rani nods, still carrying the words.

options.text: "Well, maybe we'll all need to be more careful from now on."
options.then: Rani's face falls. She hears it as blame.

options.text: "Don't listen to anyone. Just go to sleep."
options.then: Rani curls up, but doesn't sleep.

options.then: Rani closes her eyes. "Okay."

options.text: "You won't feel bad. It's all over now."
options.then: Rani is quiet. She doesn't believe it.

options.text: "Let's not talk about bad feelings. Think happy things."
options.then: Rani nods, and keeps the feelings to herself.

options.text: "Yes, but you'll need to be strong now."
options.then: Rani nods, trying hard to look strong.

steps.why: A permanent open door supports healing far more than silence.

scenarios.relearn: Affirm a child's bravery and blamelessness and your permanent open door; that supports healing far more than silence.

scenarios.hook: Driving home from a party, your daughter Sana, 15, stares out of the window for a long time.
scenarios.setup: The radio is off and the road is quiet.

steps.prompt: Sana asks: "If something bad ever happened, would you actually freak out?"

options.text: "No. I'd stay calm, believe you and help you."
options.then: Sana glances at you. "You say that now."

options.text: "Honestly? I'd probably lose it completely."
options.then: Sana laughs flatly. "Yeah. That's what I thought."

options.text: "Depends. Did something happen tonight?"
options.then: Sana shrugs. "No. Just asking."

options.text: "Nothing bad will happen if you follow my rules."
options.then: Sana rolls her eyes and looks back out of the window.

steps.prompt: Sana asks: "Even if I'd broken a rule, like going somewhere I shouldn't?"

options.text: "Even then. If someone hurt you, it's never your fault."
options.then: Sana is quiet a moment. "Okay."

options.text: "Well, then we'd have to talk about the rules first."
options.then: Sana goes quiet. "Right."

options.text: "Then you'd have learned your lesson, wouldn't you?"
options.then: Sana turns away. "Forget I asked."

options.text: "Why? Have you been going places I don't know about?"
options.then: "See? This is why I don't tell you things."

steps.why: Broken rules never make harm a child's fault. Knowing that keeps her door open to you.

steps.prompt: After a long pause, Sana says: "My friend Tanya has a problem, but she can't tell her parents."

options.text: "I'm glad you told me. Can we help her together?"
options.then: Sana nods slowly. "Maybe she could talk to you."

options.text: "Stay away from her. She sounds like trouble."
options.then: Sana crosses her arms. "She's my best friend."

options.text: "Tell me everything. Who's hurting her?"
options.then: Sana stiffens. "I shouldn't have said anything."

options.text: "That's for her parents to sort out. Don't get involved."
options.then: Sana shrugs. "They're the problem."

steps.why: Staying calm and glad when she brings something hard proves your promise.

scenarios.relearn: Tell a child in advance you'd stay calm, believe them, and help; that promise makes you the adult they can tell.

scenarios.hook: At your son's cricket practice, another dad, Manoj, mentions a news story and looks worried.
scenarios.setup: You stand together by the boundary rope.

steps.prompt: Manoj says: "If something happened to my kid, I wouldn't even know who to call."

options.text: "Save these: Childline 1098, cybercrime 1930 and 112."
options.then: Manoj pulls out his phone. "Say them again, slowly?"

options.text: "Just search online if something ever happens."
options.then: Manoj nods. "Yeah. I'll figure it out then."

options.text: "The police. That's all you need to know."
options.then: Manoj nods. "Right. Police for everything, then."

options.text: "Don't worry. That kind of thing only happens in the news."
options.then: Manoj looks relieved. "True. Our boys are fine."

steps.why: Childline 1098 for a child at risk, cybercrime 1930 for online harm, 112 in danger. The police help too.

steps.prompt: A minute later, Manoj asks: "What if it's online, like a stranger messaging him?"

options.text: "Keep the messages, then report to cybercrime 1930."
options.then: Manoj types it in. "Keep them. Got it."

options.text: "Delete the app and change his number straight away."
options.then: "That would stop it, right?" Manoj asks.

options.text: "Take his phone away for good."
options.then: Manoj frowns. "He'd just use a friend's."

options.text: "Block the person, and then just forget about it."
options.then: "Simple enough," Manoj says.

steps.why: Keeping evidence and reporting to cybercrime 1930 is how you get help to stop online harm.

steps.prompt: Manoj asks: "And if he said someone hurt him? What would I say?"

options.text: "Tell him you believe him and it's not his fault."
options.then: Manoj nods slowly. "Believe him first. Okay."

options.text: "Ask him for every detail so the police have it."
options.then: "Makes sense," Manoj says, unsure.

options.text: "Ask him if he's sure before you do anything."
options.then: Manoj nods. "Yeah. Kids exaggerate."

options.text: "Go straight to that person and sort them out."
options.then: Manoj clenches his fist. "I would, trust me."

steps.why: Children very rarely make this up. Believe him, don't blame, leave questions to professionals, then call 1098.

scenarios.relearn: The helpline card is Childline 1098, cybercrime 1930 for online, and 112 in immediate danger. Save them now.

scenarios.hook: Your son Montu whispers that Babulal-ji, who has minded the children for years while you work, hurts him.
scenarios.setup: It's late, and the others are asleep.

steps.prompt: Montu says: "He said you'd never believe me over him."

options.text: "I believe you. I'm so glad you told me."
options.then: Montu starts to cry quietly. "I didn't know how to say it."

options.text: "But he's minded you for years. Are you sure?"
options.then: Montu turns away. "See? I knew it."

options.text: "What exactly did he do? Tell me everything."
options.then: Montu pulls the sheet over his head.

options.text: "Shh. We'll talk about it in the morning."
options.then: Montu goes quiet, but you can tell he's awake.

steps.why: Believe him, even about someone long trusted. Respectability isn't safety.

steps.prompt: Montu asks: "Am I in trouble?"

options.text: "Not at all. None of this is your fault."
options.then: Montu wipes his nose. "He said it was."

options.text: "No, but you should have told me sooner."
options.then: Montu's face crumples. "I'm sorry."

options.text: "Let's not tell anyone. Then no one's in trouble."
options.then: Montu nods, confused.

options.text: "You're not. But don't go near him again, okay?"
options.then: "But who'll watch us?" he asks.

steps.why: He must hear he's not in trouble. The fault is entirely the adult's.

steps.prompt: Montu asks: "Do I have to go to his house tomorrow?"

options.text: "No. I'll keep you safe and call 1098 for help."
options.then: Montu nods and curls up against you.

options.text: "Yes, just this once. I have to go to work."
options.then: Montu goes very still and says nothing.

options.text: "No. And I'll go and shout at him first thing."
options.then: Montu looks frightened. "He'll be so angry."

options.text: "No. Your aunty will mind you from now on."
options.then: Montu relaxes. "Does he still mind Pinky next door?"

steps.why: Keep him away from the man and report it to 1098, so other children are protected too.

scenarios.relearn: Believe a child even about a trusted, long-known adult, since respectability isn't safety; reassure and protect them.

scenarios.hook: Your daughter Diya, 8, starts telling you what her tuition sir did. You feel horror rising in your face.
scenarios.setup: You breathe out slowly before you speak.

steps.prompt: Diya stops and asks: "Are you angry at me?"

options.text: "I'm not upset with you at all. I'm right here."
options.then: Diya relaxes a little. "He said not to tell."

options.text: "Oh my God! How could this happen to you?"
options.then: Diya starts crying. "I'm sorry. I'm sorry."

options.text: "Not at you. I'm furious at him!"
options.then: Diya shrinks. "Will you fight him?"

options.text: "I'm absolutely fine. Just keep going, quickly."
options.then: Diya hesitates, then talks faster, watching your face.

steps.why: A calm, steady voice tells her she didn't cause your distress, so she keeps talking.

steps.prompt: Diya says: "He said it was a game, but I didn't like it."

options.text: "Thank you for telling me. It's not your fault."
options.then: Diya nods, and her shoulders drop.

options.text: "What kind of game? What did he do?"
options.then: Diya freezes and looks away.

options.text: "Why did you keep playing it if you didn't like it?"
options.then: Diya's eyes fill. "I didn't know how to stop."

options.text: "Let's not think about it anymore, okay?"
options.then: Diya goes quiet, the rest unsaid.

steps.why: Thank her and say it's not her fault. Don't question her for details.

steps.prompt: Diya asks: "Do I have to see him again?"

options.text: "No. I'll keep you safe and call Childline 1098."
options.then: Diya hugs you tight. "Okay."

options.text: "We'll see. Classes are paid till March."
options.then: Diya goes pale.

options.text: "Only if I'm sitting right there in the room with you."
options.then: Diya nods, but squeezes your hand hard.

options.text: "No, and I'm going round there right now."
options.then: Diya grabs you. "Don't leave me!"

steps.why: Keep her away from him and call Childline 1098. That's how you keep her safe.

scenarios.relearn: Catch the horror; keep your tone calm and steady so the child keeps talking and never feels they caused your distress.

scenarios.hook: After a parents' talk on child safety, your wife Shalini admits she'd panic if a child ever told her.
scenarios.setup: You're both on the balcony after dinner.

steps.prompt: Shalini asks: "What would you even do first?"

options.text: "Believe them first. Then stay calm."
options.then: She nods slowly. "Believe first. Okay."

options.text: "Get every detail first. Calm can come after."
options.then: Shalini frowns. "Wouldn't that scare them?"

options.text: "Call the police straight away, before anything else."
options.then: "Before even talking to them?" she asks.

options.text: "Honestly, I'd just go and deal with the person."
options.then: "And leave the child alone?" she asks.

steps.why: Believing the child first, and staying calm, keeps them talking.

steps.prompt: Shalini asks: "What if I start crying? I'd want to scream."

options.text: "Breathe, keep your voice steady, cry later."
options.then: She smiles faintly. "I can try that."

options.text: "That's natural. Let them see how upset you are."
options.then: "Wouldn't that frighten them?" she wonders.

options.text: "Then let me handle it. You stay out of it."
options.then: "But what if they come to me?" she asks.

options.text: "Just don't react. Pretend it's nothing."
options.then: She shakes her head. "They'd feel it."

steps.why: A steady voice tells a child they didn't cause your distress.

steps.prompt: Shalini asks: "What do we say to them, word for word?"

options.text: "I believe you. It's not your fault. I'm glad you told me. I'll keep you safe."
options.then: She repeats it twice, quietly, until it sticks.

options.text: "Why didn't you tell us sooner? We'd have helped you straight away."
options.then: Shalini pauses. "Would that make them feel bad?"

options.text: "Don't worry. This stays our secret. Nobody else needs to know."
options.then: "Is that a promise we could keep?" she asks.

options.text: "Tell me everything, from the very beginning. Take all the time you need."
options.then: "All of it? Right then?" she asks.

steps.why: Those words say belief, no blame, thanks and protection, all at once.

steps.prompt: Shalini asks: "And after that? Who do we call?"

options.text: "Childline 1098. They guide us on reporting."
options.then: She saves the number there and then.

options.text: "No one. We'd handle it inside the family."
options.then: "Even if it was family?" she asks quietly.

options.text: "We'd confront the person first, then decide."
options.then: "Wouldn't that warn them?" she asks.

options.text: "We'd wait a few days, just to be sure."
options.then: "Sure of what, though?" she asks.

steps.why: Acting and reporting, with Childline's guidance, is the last step of the sequence.

steps.prompt: Shalini says: "I'm scared we'll get it wrong when it matters."

options.text: "Let's practise it together, right now."
options.then: She laughs nervously, then nods. "Okay. You be the child first."

options.text: "We won't get it wrong. Stop worrying."
options.then: She shrugs, not convinced.

options.text: "Let's hope we never need any of this."
options.then: "Hope isn't a plan," she says softly.

options.text: "Then leave it to me when the time comes."
options.then: "And if you're not home?" she asks.

steps.why: Preparing together despite the fear is what makes you ready when it counts.
